name: Impeccable
author: Paul Bakaus
note_o: Standout is difficulty and code craft — a real multi-engine detector (browser-injected DOM, regex, static-HTML CSS-cascade resolution, screenshot contrast) plus a live browser session layer whose helpers are built as dependency-injected factories with quota-safe localStorage wrappers, WCAG pt-to-px constants derived in a comment, and a rule exception (BORDER_SAFE_TAGS re-allowing <label>) justified against a named test matrix; weakest is organization/completeness, where a 501KB live-browser.js and a 252KB checks.mjs sit beside 24 commands and a degraded/ folder, and no worked example with real input and output is shipped.
note_c: Difficulty stands out in the substantial browser detector and durable live-browser session machinery, while completeness is weakest because the dossier shows extensive setup and commands but no end-to-end worked run.

name: Motion Graphics
author: HeyGen
note_o: Standout is ingenuity in grounding/locate.mjs — it dissolves the need for any object-detection API by exploiting that the model is bad at pixel regression but good at 'which numbered strip', drawing an ffmpeg-rendered 9x9 then 6x6 grid and reconstructing the box geometrically with a mandatory mark-and-verify step, zero npm deps; weakest is code polish, with a hand-rolled arg parser that mis-handles bare flags and a hardcoded /tmp/locate-font.ttf, against otherwise disciplined work like bake-basemap.mjs resolving Chrome dynamically and failing fast on NaN env.
note_c: Ingenuity stands out in freezing nondeterministic map imagery while retaining editable SVG overlays and grid-based image localization, while organization is weakest because the broad workflow spans many tightly coupled references; it also silently updates skills before use.

name: xlsx
author: Anthropic
note_o: Standout is code quality and difficulty together: helpers/__init__.py's opc_target normalizes OPC relationship targets and raises on package escape, safe_extract rejects symlink entries and traversal, rezip writes [Content_Types].xml first as ZIP_STORED then mkstemp+os.replace for an atomic permission-preserving swap, and soffice.py detects a blocked AF_UNIX socket at runtime and compiles an LD_PRELOAD C shim that reroutes socket() to socketpair() with per-FD bookkeeping and a pipe to wake a fake accept() — plus SKILL.md's hard-won traps (`_xlfn.` prefix for exactly six post-2007 functions, XLOOKUP/FILTER/UNIQUE banned because openpyxl writes no spill metadata and recalc still reports total_errors: 0 on the truncated result, `errors_found` exiting 0 so a clean exit is not a clean workbook); weakest is organization — a skill named xlsx ships 47 files that have nothing to do with spreadsheets (pptx_chart.py, pptx_slide.py, pptx_theme.py, validators/docx.py, validators/redlining.py and ~1MB of ISO-29500 XSDs) with no map explaining them, while SKILL.md references only recalc.py and soffice.py.
note_c: Its standout is production-grade file-handling judgment, including safe OOXML extraction, atomic rezip, and LibreOffice sandbox handling; its weakest is completeness only insofar as a few heavyweight runtime dependencies remain environment-dependent.

name: remotion-maps
author: Remotion
note_o: Standout is difficulty and code — deterministic per-frame output from nondeterministic map/tile rendering via delayRender/continueRender, a camera-path pipeline (haversine arc-length resample, moving-average smoothing chosen over Douglas-Peucker with the reason written down: 'that concentrates curvature at sparse control points to corners'), Chaikin corner-cutting with antimeridian longitude unwrapping, and turf border slicing into per-segment MultiLineStrings with cumulative lengths; weakest is completeness/organization, since prep-geo.mjs needs the user's own geodata at a hardcoded ../geodata with config edited inside the file, and render-stability.md is copied verbatim into three technique directories (deliberately, per the self-containment rule, but still triplicated).
note_c: Standout ingenuity is the deterministic pre-baking and arc-length path processing that avoids unstable live map geometry in video renders; weakest completeness is that adapting the geo-prep workflows still requires locally supplied geodata and API keys.

name: Zeroize Audit
author: Trail of Bits
note_o: Standout is difficulty: proving a wipe was removed requires emitting LLVM IR and assembly at O0/O1/O2 (plus Rust MIR and drop-glue), diffing them, and gating OPTIMIZED_AWAY_ZEROIZE on that compiler evidence rather than source inspection — with a separate 5c-poc-verifier agent checking each generated PoC actually proves its claimed finding; weakest is completeness, since the toolchain (clang, cargo +nightly, uv, uvx/Serena MCP, compile_commands.json) is heavy and no worked run with real input and output is shipped, and analyze_cfg.py's brace-counting line parser is the one soft spot in otherwise disciplined code.
note_c: Difficulty is exceptional in its multi-phase source, IR, assembly, CFG, and PoC pipeline, while the claimed control-flow assurance exceeds the shown regex-based simplified source CFG parser.

name: brainstorming
author: Jesse Vincent (obra)
note_o: Standout is difficulty: server.cjs implements RFC 6455 by hand (accept-key SHA1, masked-frame enforcement, 126/127 extended lengths with a 10MB cap) paired with a client reconnect state machine — exponential backoff, a 15s tombstone overlay, and reload-through-the-keyed-bootstrap on recovery — plus a per-session key chosen specifically because a Host/Origin allowlist cannot defeat DNS rebinding; weakest is code only relatively, where a 25KB single server file and a hardcoded remote brand-image URL with telemetry sit alongside otherwise mergeable work.
note_c: Standout code/difficulty: the browser companion implements WebSocket framing, session-key handling, reconnect backoff, and a recovery UI; weakest completeness: its multi-file runtime has substantial setup behavior but no shipped end-to-end verification or dependency setup.

name: DOCX
author: Anthropic
note_o: Standout is difficulty — merge_runs.py coalesces adjacent <w:r> runs namespace-agnostically while honoring xml:space rendering semantics and refusing to merge across <w:ins>/<w:del> wrappers (which would collapse separate revisions), and helpers/ defends the untrusted-archive path with symlink rejection, zip-slip checks and OPC target normalization; weakest is code only by a hair, because accept_changes.py returns the 'Successfully accepted all tracked changes' string on subprocess.TimeoutExpired, reporting success at exactly the failure a user hits, and merge_runs swallows every exception into a message tuple.
note_c: The standout is technical complexity in safely manipulating OOXML revisions, comments, schemas, and ZIP contents, while completeness is weakest because the workflow depends on several external desktop and CLI tools.

name: extract-web-content
author: Xin (applicant)
note_o: Standout is difficulty — real invariants are maintained (SSRF blocking via getaddrinfo + is_global on every redirect, a static-first quality gate that decides when to escalate to Playwright, bounded pagination/scrolls, an exit-code contract 0/2/3/4/5/6, and a regression test named test_nested_boilerplate_decomposition_keeps_traversal_valid that encodes a real traversal bug); weakest is organization, where six committed scripts/extract_web_content.egg-info/ build artifacts sit as orphans and extract_web.py is a single 37KB module mixing fetch I/O with parsing logic.
note_c: The standout is a security-conscious static-first extractor with bounded rendering, SSRF checks, provenance, adapters, and fixtures; the weakest point is that the central extraction module is large enough to dilute otherwise clean separation.

name: ingest-web-feeds
author: Xin (applicant)
note_o: Standout is difficulty: real invariants are held (stable_id survives content revision while version_hash changes, conditional-GET 304 with sha256 raw-artifact reuse, DTD/entity and XML-depth rejection, SSRF host/IP blocking through a custom _SafeRedirectHandler, bounded reads) and all of them are pinned by tests; weakest is ingenuity, since feed ingestion is a well-charted problem and the originality is confined to the identity split and the deliberate hand-off boundary to extract-web-content.
note_c: Standout: it combines bounded fetching, SSRF/DTD defenses, stable-versus-version identity, conditional GET state, and focused fixture tests; weakest: the large feed library is a single 33KB module and the shipped guidance lacks a concrete end-to-end output example.

name: Lark Sheets
author: Lark Suite
note_o: Standout is code and ingenuity together: lark_detect_subtables.py parses an annotated-CSV protocol where a `[row=N]` prefix can legally appear inside an open quoted field, resolves it with RFC-4180 quote parity, then refuses to proceed when the parsed rows disagree with the server-reported row_indices rather than silently profiling a short grid — and the SKILL.md's "❌ 不存在（会被 cobra 拒）" column encodes the command names agents actually hallucinate as first-class content; weakest is organization, where a 36KB entry doc carries the routing table that its 20 reference files are supposed to relieve.
note_c: Product judgment stands out in type-preserving writes, minimal-change rules, and mandatory read-back verification, while completeness is constrained by a required external CLI/sibling skill and many referenced files not included in the dossier text.

name: Media Use
author: HeyGen
note_o: Standout is ingenuity — collapsing eight media types into one `resolve` verb over a provider cascade, plus the 'media opportunity pass' with a signal-to-offer table and explicit anti-nagware constraints (grounded not generic, once per project, surface never silently mutate, because a gray-world correction ruins an intentional sunset) is a novel framing, and mapWithConcurrency is documented against two real OOM incident reports; weakest is product scope, because 'the single skill for every media need' spans 132 files with audio docs living in both references/audio.md and audio/references/, which is a platform rather than a cut scope.
note_c: The standout is the unified resolve abstraction with bounded-concurrency and provider-fallback implementation, while completeness is weakest because several media providers and local model dependencies remain environment-dependent.

name: PPTX
author: Anthropic
note_o: Standout is code quality and difficulty together — `helpers/__init__.py` resolves OPC relationship targets with explicit package-escape checks, `safe_extract` rejects symlink entries and zip-slip paths, `rezip` writes through `mkstemp` + `os.replace` with mode preservation and stores `[Content_Types].xml` uncompressed first, `add_slide.py` performs every piece of package bookkeeping (content-types, fresh rIds, `<p:sldIdLst>` insertion, stripping the notesSlide rel so notes are not shared) and `clean.py` raises `RefusedToClean` rather than deleting every slide when `<p:sldIdLst>` fails to parse, all backed by bundled ISO-IEC 29500 XSDs and a validator suite; weakest is organization, since the 20KB SKILL.md carries gotchas, edit workflows, and a color-palette design essay at once, and a ~1MB schema tree sits inside the skill directory.
note_c: Standout is difficulty: the shipped tooling maintains OOXML package relationships, safe extraction, atomic rezipping, and validation around failure-prone slide edits; weakest is completeness because several required runtimes and library assumptions remain environment-dependent.

name: pr-to-video
author: HeyGen
note_o: Standout is code and difficulty — real Node modules over a lib/ layer (storyboard parser, frame-contract validator, dimensions, tokens, transition registry) turning LLM-authored frames into a deterministic timeline with track-lane collision rules, auto-repair vs hard-fail guards run in the same pass that reads each frame, paginated gh api so a big PR doesn't truncate at 100 files, and a regression test that keeps 'bgm_pending' distinguishable from 'silent by design' so a silent film can't ship by accident; weakest is completeness, since running it requires the whole external HyperFrames ecosystem (npx hyperframes CLI, gh auth, HeyGen sign-in) plus sibling skills reached by relative path (../hyperframes-core, ../media-use) that are not in this directory.
note_c: Standout is a carefully contracted PR-to-video pipeline with deterministic ingestion, frame/audio invariants, failure gates, and regression tests; weakest is its substantial dependency on a wider HyperFrames installation and sibling skills.

name: gemini
author: Xin (applicant)
note_o: Difficulty is the standout — live-SPA browser automation with ordered selector-candidate lists, base64 prompt passing to dodge AppleScript escaping, and a done-detector built on reply-count plus text-length stability precisely because the author discovered Gemini's 'Stop response' button is present even at idle; completeness is weakest, since SKILL.md itself warns the selectors are a 'best-effort first pass' and tells the reader to run doctor+probe and fix any n:0 group before trusting `ask`.
note_c: The standout is robust browser automation—candidate selectors, DOM probing, response-stability waiting, and deterministic Markdown reconstruction—while completeness is limited by a macOS/Chrome-only setup and selectors explicitly acknowledged to drift.

name: Caveman Compress
author: Julius Brussee
note_o: Standout is difficulty — validate.py extracts headings, fenced blocks (CommonMark-correct: variable fence length, nested fences, indentation-aware), URLs, paths and inline code from both versions and diffs them, then compress.py cherry-picks targeted fixes rather than recompressing, which is deterministic verification of a nondeterministic LLM rewrite plus a real fence parser; weakest is completeness, because benchmark.py globs `parents[3]/tests/caveman-compress` for `*.original.md` fixtures that are not shipped and whose comment's path walk does not match the plugins/caveman/skills layout.
note_c: The standout is ingenuity in combining exact-preservation validators, targeted retries, atomic writes, and out-of-tree backups, while completeness is weakest because the Claude runtime dependency and end-to-end setup are not fully specified.

name: slide-making
author: Xin (applicant)
note_o: Standout is difficulty: the tikz-audit convergence loop maintains real invariants — stale-render guard by comparing pdf/tex mtimes, algebraic clearance pre-check (physical_gap = dist * scale vs max text width) that kills a defect class before any render, fixers writing JSON patch files instead of editing so a single sequential apply_patches.py pass validates old_string uniqueness, rejects overlapping spans, and applies bottom-up to preserve offsets; weakest is completeness/consistency — the 28KB tikz-audit doc reuses gate IDs G9 and G10 for two different checks each, the G10 table row has its '~30s per fix wave' cell in the wrong column, and it prescribes `stat -c %Y` (GNU) in a document that elsewhere warns about macOS behavior, alongside hardcoded /tmp paths throughout.
note_c: Its standout is difficult, original operational design—the manifest/live-route model and file-mediated TikZ audit convergence are concrete mechanisms—while reproducibility is weaker because substantial external rendering and agent prerequisites are not fully specified.

name: web-templates
author: Xin (applicant)
note_o: Standout is product judgment — the 'Non-negotiables' section encodes corrections the user already made once (left nav routes to short pages, no <details> accordion stacks, icons align to the title line, measure with getBoundingClientRect) so they are never re-earned, and the pick-one table cuts scope to exactly two site shapes; weakest is difficulty, since under the polish it is conventional hash-router SPA work (esc/slug/el helpers are copy-pasted across both templates) with no invariant a strong engineer would stall on.
note_c: The standout is product judgment: the two deliberately opinionated templates encode a specific review workflow and real usability corrections, while completeness is weakest because rebuild generation is required but no generator is shipped.

name: Skill Creator
author: Anthropic
note_o: Standout is ingenuity — framing skill authoring as an A/B eval loop that always spawns a paired baseline arm (no-skill for new skills, a cp -r snapshot of the old skill for edits) and separately optimizes the description against a train/holdout split, with aggregate_benchmark.py reporting stddev across repeated runs; weakest is organization, since the 33KB SKILL.md is a monolithic entry doc that breaks the under-500-line progressive-disclosure rule it teaches, and assets/eval_review.html sits beside eval-viewer/viewer.html with no stated precedence.
note_c: The standout is the paired with-skill versus baseline evaluation loop with quantitative aggregation and review UI, while organization is weakest because a very large SKILL.md carries material that could be progressively disclosed.

name: Remotion Best Practices
author: Remotion
note_o: Standout is difficulty — prep-cesium-path.mjs does haversine arc-length resampling, moving-average smoothing chosen over Douglas-Peucker with the reason stated (simplification concentrates curvature at sparse control points and produces corners), plus a damping dial toward the straight chord, and flight-path.ts adds Chaikin corner-cutting with antimeridian longitude unwrapping; weakest is organization, because the entire remotion-maps subtree is duplicated verbatim under remotion-markup/remotion-maps/ — roughly thirty files including a 333KB country-meta.json shipped twice — with no statement of which copy is canonical.
note_c: The standout is real geometry and rendering-support code, especially deterministic smoothing, antimeridian handling, and pre-baked map data decisions; the weakest is reproducibility because the extensive routed reference tree includes environment- and data-specific techniques without one end-to-end setup path.

name: chatgpt
author: Xin (applicant)
note_o: Standout is ingenuity/difficulty — it reads replies by clicking ChatGPT's own Copy button and lifting the clipboard (clean Markdown instead of innerText scraping), calls /backend-api from inside the logged-in page with the Bearer token from /api/auth/session instead of scraping the virtualized sidebar, base64-pipes prompts through AppleScript to dodge escaping, and harvest_cookies.py correctly implements Chrome v10 AES-128-CBC + the v127 32-byte domain-hash prefix; weakest is organization, because a live .pw-profile Chromium profile (995 files, Cookies DB and cache, an authenticated session) is committed inside the skill directory and dominates it.
note_c: Standout is the resilient live-site automation strategy—base64 prompt transfer, API pagination, copy-button capture, and recovery paths—while the bundled 999-file Chrome profile and machine-specific backend weaken shipping hygiene.

name: General Video
author: HeyGen
note_o: Standout is ingenuity: requiring each parallel frame-worker to emit a motion.json sidecar declaring its measured entry/exit vector so the orchestrator can stamp seams and a numeric gate fails loudly on a lie is a genuinely stealable way to make independently-generated scenes composable; weakest is completeness, because nothing runs from this directory alone — frame-packets.mjs imports ../../hyperframes-core, and the workflow depends on npx hyperframes, /media-use, and /figma, none of them shipped.
note_c: Standout: the scene-packet boundary, shared-core wrapper with a deliberate design-truth delta, atomic-overflow test, and motion seam sidecar show unusually disciplined production design; weakest: much of the workflow depends on a large external HyperFrames skill hierarchy rather than self-contained runnable material.

name: MCP Builder
author: Anthropic
note_o: Standout is ingenuity backed by real code: it inverts the quality metric ('the measure of an MCP server is NOT how comprehensively it implements tools' but whether an LLM with only those tools can answer 10 hard, keyword-unsearchable, stable-answer questions) and ships the harness for it -- connections.py abstracts stdio/SSE/streamable-HTTP behind one AsyncExitStack context manager that tears down correctly on `BaseException` and handles the 2- vs 3-tuple transport result, while evaluation.py runs the agent loop and also collects the model's own `<feedback>` on the tool schemas; weakest is completeness, which still needs the reader to infer the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and inspector setup, and evaluation.py's `except Exception` around every tool call plus the parse function that swallows errors into `[]` are the only soft spots in otherwise mergeable code.
note_c: Organization stands out in separating protocol guidance, language guides, evaluation guidance, and reusable multi-transport connection code; ingenuity is weakest because the implementation and evaluation approach are solid but largely conventional MCP practice.

name: paper-coread
author: Xin (applicant)
note_o: Standout is ingenuity/product: freezing fresh-eyes questions BEFORE the deep read and treating an unresolved one as a finding (OPEN status) is a real inversion, and the 'never repeat the paper's vagueness — write the equation yourself and mark it INFERRED' rule shows a second pass by a named user; weakest is organization, a 27k monolithic SKILL.md that has absorbed block-by-block corrections ('do not add a separate logical-spine box') that belong in references/.
note_c: Standout ingenuity/product judgment: freezing abstract-only questions before the read and surfacing data caveats create a genuinely reader-specific research workflow; weakest completeness: the crop utility depends on undeclared platform tools and the page-production process remains largely manual.

name: pdf-to-md
author: Xin (applicant)
note_o: Product judgment is the standout — zero-config default (`--use-llm` deliberately off), auto-bootstrapping venv, a named fallback (pymupdf4llm) with its limits stated, and QA greps that warn a `$$`-count of 0 can be legitimate rather than a dropped equation; difficulty is weakest, as pdf2md.sh is a 65-line flag-mapping wrapper around one `marker_single` call plus a sed/perl image strip, with no point that would stop a strong engineer.
note_c: The standout is unusually sharp product judgment around academic-PDF fidelity, including the born-digital fast-path trade-off and practical QA, while the weakest point is reproducibility because heavyweight unpinned dependencies and an Apple-Silicon MPS default are assumed.

name: deploy-to-vercel
author: Vercel Labs
note_o: Standout is product judgment: preview-not-production by default, an explicit ask before git push, per-host branches for Claude Code vs claude.ai vs Codex, and hard-won traps documented with reasons ("Do NOT use vercel project inspect... with --yes, silently link as a side-effect"; "Do not curl or fetch the deployed URL to verify"); weakest is code, since deploy.sh and deploy-codex.sh are near-identical 8.8KB copies differing mainly in DEPLOY_ENDPOINT, with framework detection done by grepping package.json text rather than parsing JSON.
note_c: Product judgment is strongest in preview-by-default, team-aware branching, and explicit consent before git push, while code quality is softened by duplicated long framework-detection scripts relying on loose text matching.

name: Writing Skills
author: Jesse Vincent (obra)
note_o: Standout is ingenuity: reframing skill authoring as TDD — run the pressure scenario first, record the agent's exact rationalizations as the failing test, then write only enough prose to close those loopholes — plus the empirically-derived SDO finding that a description summarizing the workflow makes the agent follow the description and skip the body (documented with the one-review-instead-of-two case); weakest is organization/product, a 26KB SKILL.md that violates its own '<500 words' rule, overlaps the bundled 46KB anthropic-best-practices.md, and leaves persuasion-principles.md as an orphan, while render-graphs.js parses digraph bodies with a brace regex that a '}' inside a label would break.
note_c: Standout ingenuity: it reframes skill writing as pressure-tested TDD and identifies description text as a discovery shortcut that can bypass instructions; weakest completeness: the Graphviz renderer documents its dependency but the skill shows no executed test results for its own prescribed subagent evaluations.

name: optimize-token-usage
author: Xin (applicant)
note_o: Standout is product judgment — the Stop hook is silent when healthy, debounced by a +10pt hysteresis with a per-transcript state file that resets on a new session, and all thresholds are env-tunable (CTX_EARLY_FRAC/CLAUDE_CONTEXT_WINDOW) rather than requiring code edits; weakest is completeness, since context_guard.py depends on a settings.json Stop-hook entry the skill only describes rather than ships, and the transcript-parsing loop is duplicated verbatim between the two scripts.
note_c: Standout product judgment: the silent, debounced stop hook names a concrete MCP culprit at actionable thresholds; weakest completeness: it has no shipped hook configuration or worked transcript/output example.

name: soal-connect
author: Xin (applicant)
note_o: Standout is difficulty: connect.sh + ssh_master.exp + vpn_connect.applescript chain Cisco GUI automation, expect-driven Duo 2FA, and an SSH ControlMaster socket into one idempotent pipeline that reuses a live master and polls for real connectivity when the GUI stalls; weakest is product judgment, because identity is baked in (USER_NAME="xinzeng", Duo option 3 = one specific iPhone, /share/data/ben_snowflake default) so nobody but the author can run it.
note_c: The standout is a real VPN→Duo→SSH ControlMaster recovery pipeline with explicit handoffs, while code quality is limited by machine-specific identities and unsafe interpolation of remote-control arguments into an unquoted heredoc.

name: PDF
author: Anthropic
note_o: Standout is ingenuity tied to real difficulty — the non-fillable-form path closes a verification loop the model can actually see (extract_form_structure infers labels/lines/checkboxes, check_bounding_boxes rejects overlapping rects and entries shorter than their font size, create_validation_image draws red entry and blue label boxes onto the rendered page), and fill_fillable_fields monkeypatches pypdf's get_inherited to unwrap paired /Opt values, a fix nobody writes without hitting it; weakest is completeness, since SKILL.md points at REFERENCE.md/FORMS.md while the shipped files are lowercase, fill_fillable_fields.py imports extract_form_field_info by bare module name (requiring cwd to be scripts/), and no dependency is pinned or manifested.
note_c: Standout difficulty: the scripts inspect annotation hierarchies, form geometry, and field-value validity rather than merely calling a converter; weakest product judgment: the entry guide is a broad PDF toolbox with little opinion about a primary user workflow.

name: Vercel React Best Practices
author: Vercel Labs
note_o: Code is the standout — 70 rule files each carrying a precise incorrect/correct TSX pair on real React hazards (useEffectEvent excluded from deps, handler-in-ref for stable subscriptions, module-level didInit guard against remount, RSC serialization boundaries), and the corpus is a compiled artifact where the filename prefix is the section taxonomy so IDs auto-generate; completeness is the weakest, with README documenting pnpm build/validate/extract-tests against a src/ directory and test-cases.json that are not in the shipped skill, and metadata.json still claiming '40+ rules' where SKILL.md says 70.
note_c: Organization stands out in the impact-ranked, individually addressable React rules with concrete bad/good examples; the claimed pnpm build, validation, and extraction workflow is weakest because its scripts and package files are absent from the inventory.

name: Prototype
author: Emil Kowalski
note_o: Standout is ingenuity plus product — 'the picker is chrome, not a contestant' freezes the harness design verbatim so it can never be confused with the work being judged, variants must each declare a named divergence axis before any code is written (and one gets cut if two converge), and the CSS earns its exceptions out loud (the `width` transition is allowed because the element is 28px, absolutely positioned, and has no layout dependents; `data-ready` gates the slide so first paint does not animate; reduced-motion and focus-visible both handled); weakest is difficulty — a variant picker plus an isolated prototype route is careful front-end work, not an algorithmic problem where a strong engineer would get stuck.
note_c: Forcing meaningful divergence behind a fixed, full-size picker and requiring an explicit user choice is excellent product judgment; the actual harness is specified but not shipped as a runnable artifact.

name: Lark Mail
author: Lark Suite
note_o: Standout is product judgment: every send path defaults to a draft and requires an explicit `--confirm-send`, the confirmation table is organized by reversibility (delete/trash/cancel-scheduled/rule-changes require a preview with affected count; label, read-state and folder moves do not), and there are explicit rules against fabricating message_id/folder_id when a lookup misses and against auto-responding to READ_RECEIPT_REQUEST without asking; weakest is code — the only shipped artifacts are five HTML email templates, and most are verbatim Lark-editor exports (LarkHackSafariFont inline spans, data-li-line attributes) while the one hand-authored stylesheet, research--market-report.html, builds its stat and player rows on `display:flex`, which Outlook's Word rendering engine does not support.
note_c: Its standout is product and safety judgment: untrusted-mail treatment, confirmation previews, and draft-link constraints address real failure modes; its weakest is code craft because the supplied implementation is chiefly CLI guidance and large inline-HTML templates rather than maintainable program logic.

name: Subagent-Driven Development
author: Jesse Vincent (obra)
note_o: Standout is ingenuity and product sense earned from real failures — the ledger-as-recovery-map (first line names the plan file; never read another plan's ledger; after compaction trust the ledger and git log over your own recollection) answering the named 'single most expensive failure observed', plus the 5-round fix loop with model escalation and a circuit breaker, and 'an omitted model silently inherits your session's most expensive one'; weakest is code, since the only executable artifacts are three ~1.5KB shell scripts whose contents are not present to judge and the 28KB SKILL.md carries the state machine as prose.
note_c: Product judgment stands out in plan-identified recovery ledgers and bounded review/fix loops, while code is weakest because the substantive evidence shown is workflow prose and prompts rather than executable implementation.

name: Crypto Protocol Diagram
author: Trail of Bits
note_o: Standout is completeness — two full worked examples (a typed PEP-723 X25519/Ed25519/HKDF handshake and a ProVerif model) each paired with byte-level expected ASCII and Mermaid output that the SKILL.md explicitly designates as the quality bar; weakest is organization, since the 18.8KB SKILL.md carries both the code and spec workflows inline instead of pushing them into the references it already maintains.
note_c: Standout organization: code, RFC/prose, and formal-model routes share a well-factored diagramming workflow with concrete expected outputs; weakest code quality: the only executable code is a lightly validated demonstration rather than an implemented extractor.

name: Finishing a Development Branch
author: Jesse Vincent (obra)
note_o: Standout is product judgment and ingenuity together — provenance-based cleanup (only worktrees under .worktrees/ are ours to remove), a reduced 2-option menu for detached HEAD, merge-verify-then-delete ordering, discard offered only on explicit request and gated on the literal typed word 'discard', and a Common Rationalizations table that pre-rebuts the agent's own excuses; weakest is code surface, which is roughly fifteen lines of (correct, subtly-ordered) git shell embedded in prose rather than a program, with no worked transcript.
note_c: Standout product judgment is the provenance-based worktree cleanup and exact human confirmation before destructive deletion; weakest code quality is that the careful shell logic is embedded as instructions rather than a shipped executable.

name: HyperFrames Keyframes
author: HeyGen
note_o: Standout is difficulty/ingenuity — it maintains a genuine determinism invariant for a seekable renderer (bans Date.now, performance.now, unseeded Math.random, timers and async-built timelines; requires `window.__timelines[compositionId]` to match `data-composition-id`) and pairs it with a real observability vocabulary where ghost spacing reads as velocity and 'a helper-selector shot is not proof'; weakest is code as an artifact — the JS/CSS are idiomatic snippets (correct `immediateRender: false` for later from() tweens, compositor channels over top/left/width) but nothing here is a runnable unit, and the GSAP skeleton is duplicated in SKILL.md and references/keyframe-patterns.md.
note_c: Seek-safe animation framed as a pose contract verified through focused pixel diagnostics is the standout; the runnable runtime and verification tooling are external rather than shipped.

name: Systematic Debugging
author: Jesse Vincent (obra)
note_o: Ingenuity is the standout — treating a prose skill as a system to be adversarially validated (four shipped pressure-test fixtures, plus the insight that naming the exact rationalization sentences creates cognitive friction) and the 3-failed-fixes circuit breaker that escalates to questioning the architecture rather than attempting fix #4; completeness is weakest, as condition-based-waiting-example.ts imports `~/threads/thread-manager` and `~/threads/types` from another project so it cannot compile as shipped, and find-polluter.sh hardcodes `npm test`.
note_c: The standout is the pressure-resistant debugging process—especially evidence at component boundaries and the three-failed-fixes architectural stop—while completeness is weakened by project-specific utility types and no portable setup or demonstrated run.

name: project-discovery
author: Xin (applicant)
note_o: Standout is code quality — four stdlib-only argparse CLIs sharing one output contract (JSON array to file or '-' for stdout, progress to stderr, per-query failures warn and continue so one dead source can't kill the sweep); weakest is completeness/accuracy of claims, since merge_sources.py advertises 'fuzzy name match' but actually does exact matching on a normalize() key that only strips a fixed suffix list, so 'Ether.fi' and 'EtherFi' would not merge.
note_c: The standout is the cleanly separated, usable multi-source pipeline with consistent JSON shaping; the weakest is correctness-to-claim alignment because the merge is normalized exact matching rather than fuzzy matching and the documented retry behavior is not implemented.

name: Webapp Testing
author: Anthropic
note_o: Standout is code — with_server.py validates that --server and --port counts match, polls each port with socket.create_connection until a timeout, and cleans up in a finally block that escalates terminate to kill, propagating the child's exit code; weakest is completeness, since Playwright is never declared as a prerequisite (no `playwright install chromium`) and two of the three examples write to a hardcoded /mnt/user-data/outputs/ that does not exist outside the authoring environment, and the PIPE'd server stdout/stderr are never drained so a chatty dev server can fill the pipe buffer and hang.
note_c: The standout is the practical server-lifecycle helper paired with rendered-DOM reconnaissance for real browser testing; the weakest is code robustness because shell execution and undrained piped server output make the helper fragile under untrusted commands or noisy processes.

name: Animate
author: Emil Kowalski
note_o: Product judgment is the standout — the frequency gate is designed to produce zero lines of code ('that's a success, not a dodge'), scope is cut against four named sibling skills, and the output section forbids padding into a report; difficulty is weakest because there is no executable mechanism at all, only CSS/JSX specimens, so a reader reproducing it would get stuck on nothing but taste.
note_c: The standout is the deliberate animation gate that can correctly yield no animation plus concrete interaction constraints, while the weakest is code quality because this ships guidance and snippets rather than an executable implementation.

name: Agentic Actions Auditor
author: Trail of Bits
note_o: Difficulty and product tie for standout — cross-file resolution of composite actions and reusable workflows with an order-dependent uses: classification algorithm, a fixed depth limit, and taint tracing through three env: scopes, plus scope cut explicitly via a When NOT to Use section and a documented reason for skipping the gh auth pre-check; code is the weakest since nothing is executable, only gh api/jq recipes embedded in prose.
note_c: Product judgment stands out in the one-level cross-file resolution and concrete attacker-data-flow model; code is weakest because the audit remains an agent-executed checklist rather than a parser.

name: using-git-worktrees
author: Jesse Vincent (obra)
note_o: Standout is ingenuity paired with genuinely careful shell: the submodule guard catches the exact false positive that breaks the naive detector (GIT_DIR != GIT_COMMON is also true inside a submodule, so it checks `git rev-parse --show-superproject-working-tree` before concluding 'already isolated'), the `git check-ignore` gate stops an unignored worktree directory from committing the whole tree, and 'never fight the harness' correctly prefers a native EnterWorktree tool because `git worktree add` creates phantom state the harness cannot clean up -- plus consent is asked before touching the user's repo and a sandbox permission denial falls back to working in place; weakest is code as a shipped artifact, since the mechanism exists only as ~8 inline snippets in one 6.8KB markdown file with no script, no test, and no recorded example run.
note_c: Product judgment and ingenuity stand out in native-tool-first isolation plus the linked-worktree versus submodule guard; code quality is weakest because the careful shell commands remain embedded examples rather than a packaged executable.

name: Claude API
author: Anthropic
note_o: Ingenuity is the standout — the frontmatter TRIGGER/SKIP predicate with a grep-first negative check ('run this grep FIRST if no provider named, don't Read the file') turns the description field into a routing gate, and the API-drift table names exactly which shapes now 400 (budget_tokens on Opus 5); organization is the weakest, a 72KB entry doc plus 20 overlapping shared/managed-agents-*.md files (core, overview, onboarding, api-reference) with no stated precedence.
note_c: Organization stands out through language-specific references and explicit API-drift routing; code is weakest because this is chiefly a documentation corpus with snippets, not an executable integration.

name: Hallmark
author: Hassan El Mghari (Nutlope)
note_o: Standout is ingenuity — the thesis that AI slop is structural rather than visual, enforced by stamping the chosen macrostructure into the emitted CSS (/* Hallmark · macrostructure: … */) plus a .hallmark/log.json so the next run must pick a different one, and by naming its own most-repeated output ('Specimen fall-through') as an anti-pattern in its own docs; weakest is code/organization, because nothing is executable (the 53 slop gates and the pre-emit P/H/E/S/R/V critique are self-reported, not checked), the entry SKILL.md is 67k, and macrostructures.md and macrostructures/ (likewise component-cookbook.md and components/) coexist with no stated precedence.
note_c: Standout is the product judgment in structural diversification, scoped redesign safety, and concrete responsive/a11y gates; weakest is that the extensive web guidance contains no executable implementation to validate those rules.

name: slack-gif-creator
author: Anthropic
note_o: Standout is code/difficulty — this is the only submission in the batch with a real runnable library, and gif_builder.optimize_colors solves a genuine format problem by stacking sampled frame pixels, padding them and reshaping into a synthetic near-square RGB image purely so PIL's quantize() can derive one global palette applied across all frames; weakest is the doc/code divergence — SKILL.md advertises `easing='back_out'` and tells you to use it for slide overshoot, but ease_back_in/out are defined after EASING_FUNCTIONS and never registered in it, so get_easing('back_out') silently returns linear, and validators.py swallows duration errors in a bare `except:`.
note_c: The frame builder’s palette sampling and resizing form a useful concrete pipeline; the validator claims Slack readiness while its pass condition checks dimensions rather than the stated size, duration, or FPS constraints.

name: Web Artifacts Builder
author: Anthropic
note_o: Difficulty and product tie for standout — collapsing a React+Radix+Tailwind app into one self-contained HTML file with path aliases surviving (parcel-resolver-tspaths + html-inline) is a real constraint solved, and the SKILL.md draws an explicit negative boundary ('not for simple single-file HTML/JSX artifacts') and argues testing should come after presenting because it adds latency; completeness is weakest, since init-artifact.sh hard-requires `shadcn-components.tar.gz` that is not in the shipped inventory and exits immediately without it, and it silently runs `npm install -g pnpm` plus `$SED_INPLACE` unquoted word-splitting.
note_c: The standout is a practical React-to-single-HTML build pipeline with basic environment checks, while completeness is weakest because init-artifact.sh requires shadcn-components.tar.gz although that asset is absent from the shipped inventory.

name: Improve Codebase Architecture
author: Matt Pocock
note_o: Product judgment is the standout — `disable-model-invocation: true`, writing the report to `$TMPDIR` 'so nothing lands in the repo', a hard stop at 'Do NOT propose interfaces yet' before asking which candidate to explore, and offering to record a rejection as an ADR so future runs stop re-suggesting it; completeness is weakest, since the process leans on `/codebase-design`, `/grilling`, `/domain-modeling`, `CONTEXT.md` and `docs/adr/`, none of which ship here.
note_c: The standout is product judgment: recent-change hot spots, ADR-aware recommendations, and a deliberately deferred interface-design loop target a real review moment, while the weakest is code quality because the HTML is a scaffold rather than a working report generator.

name: Lark Doc
author: Lark Suite
note_o: Standout is organization and the genre-contract idea: a 3.8KB entry doc that is pure routing with an explicit 'read each reference only on first entering that stage, never all at once' rule, and 20 genre files that each define hard constraints, allowed/banned block types, a 任一出现即失败 failure row, and disambiguation against named siblings — plus a placeholder protocol ([指标定义待核], blocked) that forbids fabrication instead of merely discouraging it; weakest is code, as all 44 shipped files are markdown wrapping an external lark-cli that is not part of the skill.
note_c: Standout organization/product judgment: the router and genre contracts sharply distinguish document intents, authority boundaries, and blocked states; weakest code quality: the files are extensive policy and CLI guidance rather than an executable implementation.

name: Improve Animations
author: Emil Kowalski
note_o: Standout is product judgment and ingenuity — the audit-then-plan split is justified by model economics (capable model where judgment compounds, cheap executor for the edit), plans are commit-stamped and written for 'zero context and zero taste' with 'use the easing discussed above' named as the forbidden phrasing, and the verification section invents a feel-check primitive (DevTools playback at 10%, toggle prefers-reduced-motion) for a property no test can assert; weakest is code, with no executable artifact and a dependency on a sibling review-animations skill that is not in this folder.
note_c: The standout is the sharply scoped audit-to-self-contained-plan handoff with exact values, code excerpts, and feel checks; the weakest is that it delegates all actual implementation rather than shipping a mechanism to perform it.

name: Audit Context Building
author: Trail of Bits
note_o: Standout is ingenuity — enforcing the context budget structurally rather than by instruction ("a subagent bound to a return schema cannot return prose"), plus `nothing found` as a first-class assumption result and the rule that conflicting records get both quoted instead of reconciled; weakest is code, since the directory ships only markdown and the dispatching command and function-analyzer agent it routes to live outside it.
note_c: Standout organization: the analysis format, domain notes, and worked example progressively make a rigorous audit workflow navigable; weakest completeness: the claimed enforcing subagents and dossier-writing workflow are absent from the inventory.

name: Lark Calendar
author: Lark Suite
note_o: Standout is product judgment — hard-won operational rules like never asking the user for a time (default a window and run +suggestion first), never letting +room-find take a fuzzy range, auto-shortening an rrule to a room's reserve_until_time, and forbidding rebuilt room_name strings in output; weakest is code, since nothing executes here — it is a manual for an unshipped lark-cli, and the 12.5KB entry doc restates the schedule-meeting routing in three separate sections.
note_c: Standout product judgment: recurrence exceptions, ambiguous times, room selection, and confirmation gates are handled as real calendar-user failure modes; weakest code evidence: the artifact is instruction and CLI documentation, with no implementation of its scheduling behavior.

name: Triage
author: Matt Pocock
note_o: Standout is product judgment and the two real inversions behind it — AGENT-BRIEF.md forbids file paths and line numbers on purpose because the brief outlives the codebase it describes (the opposite of normal spec advice), and OUT-OF-SCOPE.md bars 'already implemented' closures from the rejection KB because recording them would poison the dedup check with false rejections — plus a mandatory AI-generated disclaimer on every posted comment and an external-PR filter that is discovery-only so a named PR is still triaged; weakest is code and difficulty, since the state machine exists purely as prose with no validation of role conflicts and no executable artifact of any kind, and it depends on `setup-matt-pocock-skills` having run to supply the label mapping.
note_c: Standout is ingenuity: combining triage states with durable agent briefs and a concept-level rejected-work knowledge base turns issue handling into institutional memory; weakest is code quality because the state machine is prose, not implemented software.

name: Remotion Captions
author: Remotion
note_o: Organization is the standout — a 954-byte SKILL.md that defines the one shared `Caption` type and then routes to three task files matching three real starting states (have video / have .srt / have captions), each with its own frontmatter and cross-links; ingenuity is weakest, since the content is straightforward first-party API documentation for packages the author already ships, with no idea beyond correct usage.
note_c: The standout is progressive disclosure across transcription, SRT import, and display, with sound render-delay error handling in the examples, while the weakest is ingenuity because it primarily assembles standard Remotion APIs into documentation.

name: Teach
author: Matt Pocock
note_o: Standout is ingenuity: learning records as ADRs that compute the zone of proximal development, the fluency-vs-storage-strength split driving 'difficulty is the enemy for knowledge, the tool for skills', the glossary rule that a term is admitted only once the user can use it correctly, and quizzes whose answers must be equal length so formatting leaks no clue; weakest is code, since the promised beautiful Tufte-style HTML lessons, quiz widgets, and shared ./assets stylesheet ship as instructions with not one line of HTML or CSS included.
note_c: Standout: the mission-led persistent learning model, evidence-gated glossary promotion, and ADR-like learning records are an original and carefully scoped teaching system; weakest: despite calling for interactive HTML lessons, it ships no HTML, CSS, component, or verification implementation.

name: find-animation-opportunities
author: Emil Kowalski
note_o: Standout is ingenuity — an opportunity finder built as a rejection filter, with a mandatory 'Rejected candidates' section called out as 'what separates this skill from an animation wishlist', a frequency table where 100+/day is a hard disqualifier not a judgment call (Raycast's no-animation command palette cited as optimal), and a closed enum of purposes from which 'it looks cool' is deliberately absent; weakest is code and difficulty, as it ships one 9.5KB markdown file with no mechanism, and its exact easing tokens live in a sibling skill's AUDIT.md that is not shipped here.
note_c: The standout is the four-part rejection gate and required rejected-candidates section, which turns restraint into an operational method; the weakest is that it contains no executable auditing artifact.

name: Prototype
author: Matt Pocock
note_o: Standout is product judgment — defaults are decided rather than configured (3 variants, capped at 5, sub-shape A on the existing route because 'an empty route hides design problems that a populated one would expose'), the ambiguous-branch case is handled for when the user is unreachable, and the throwaway is captured on a side branch when done; weakest is code/difficulty, since the whole 16KB is prose with a single 5-line pseudo-code switcher snippet and nothing to run.
note_c: The standout is product judgment in making prototypes answer one explicit question and exposing state or radically different variants, while the weakest is code because the supplied artifact is guidance and pseudocode rather than a runnable prototype.

name: Setup Matt Pocock Skills
author: Matt Pocock
note_o: Standout is product judgment — every question leads with its recommended answer so the user can accept in one word, Section B is skipped outright when `triage` is not installed and Section C when there are no monorepo signals, `AGENTS.md` is never created if `CLAUDE.md` exists, an existing `## Agent skills` block is updated in place rather than appended, and the 'PRs as a request surface' flag is defaulted off with an explicit instruction not to even raise it; weakest is code and difficulty, since nothing here executes and the hardest content is CLI recipes (the `gh api .../dependencies/blocked_by` call correctly insists on the numeric database id rather than the `#number` or `node_id`, and GitLab's `/blocked_by` quick action is caveated as Premium-tier) rather than anything a strong engineer would get stuck on.
note_c: Standout is organization: small, purpose-separated templates and explicit configuration ownership give each concern one durable home; weakest is code quality because setup is entirely prompt-directed rather than executable.

name: Domain Modeling
author: Matt Pocock
note_o: Standout is product judgment — the skill defines its own negative space ('merely reading CONTEXT.md is not this skill'), creates files lazily only when there is something to write, and gates ADRs behind three simultaneous conditions (hard to reverse, surprising without context, a real trade-off) with 'an ADR can be a single paragraph' cutting the usual template ceremony; weakest is code and difficulty — no executable artifact, and the three ADR conditions plus the single/multi-context inference rules are restated verbatim in both SKILL.md and the format files.
note_c: The three-part ADR threshold and lazy glossary creation are a sharp, opinionated workflow; its weakness is that it is entirely instructional rather than executable.

name: Vercel CLI with Tokens
author: Vercel Labs
note_o: Standout is product judgment — safe defaults chosen rather than exposed (preview unless production is explicitly asked, ask before `git push`, never curl the deployed URL), token never passed as `--token` with the reason given (shell history and process listings), and the non-obvious operational trap named: `vercel project inspect` and `vercel link` silently link or prompt so they must not be used for state detection, while `vercel ls`/`whoami` are safe; weakest is organization and code — everything is one 10KB monolithic file with no progressive disclosure, the content is copy-paste bash rather than any artifact, and the Stripe Projects plan-change section is scope creep into billing a real card.
note_c: Default-preview deployment, token handling, and avoidance of side-effectful discovery show strong operational judgment; the documented environment-variable removal command has no explicit consent gate.

name: Orca Emulator
author: Stably AI
note_o: Standout is ingenuity — the file deliberately refuses to document the command surface and instead defers to `ORCA skills get orca-emulator` so the guide can never drift from the binary that will run it, paired with the specific hard-won guard that bare `orca` on Linux resolves to the GNOME screen reader and starts speech on the user's machine, and the rule to stop rather than fall through to another executable and silently target a different build; weakest is difficulty, since as shipped it is a 3.7KB dispatch stub with no mechanism of its own.
note_c: The standout is the version-matched documentation handoff and explicit protection against launching the unrelated GNOME screen reader; the weakest is code quality because the shipped artifact is a discovery stub rather than an executable integration.

name: Apple Design
author: Emil Kowalski
note_o: Standout is ingenuity — it translates WWDC fluid-interface doctrine into exact web primitives and explicitly corrects the textbook v²/(2·decel) projection to Apple's shipped exponential-decay form, plus the relativeVelocity = gestureVelocity/(target−current) normalization and the 'decompose 2D motion into independent X and Y springs' rule; weakest is organization, a single undivided 22KB SKILL.md with twelve numbered sections and no progressive disclosure into reference files.
note_c: The standout is the concrete velocity-projection and interruptibility guidance grounded in browser primitives; the weakest is code quality because it ships illustrative fragments rather than a runnable interaction implementation.

name: HyperFrames CLI
author: HeyGen
note_o: Standout is product judgment — it writes for an agent operator and documents its own product's defects honestly ('do not rely on --strict-variables for cloudrun render-batch: the command accepts the flag but does not validate batch rows', 'doctor --json always exits zero, gate on its payload') and forbids rendering on a passing check without human approval; weakest is code, since all 98KB across 11 files is markdown documenting an external CLI with not one executable artifact shipped.
note_c: The standout is product judgment in its explicit preview-approval and privacy-preserving feedback gates, while the weakest is code because the dossier supplies CLI instructions but no CLI implementation.

name: Vulnerability Triage Brocards
author: Trail of Bits
note_o: Standout is product judgment — the skill knows its exact moment (the gate between an agentic discovery pipeline and auditor time, drawn as a mermaid flow), defaults to stopping at the first DISMISS with a full-evaluation override, and includes a Rationalizations to Reject section covering both failure directions plus the anti-padding rule that ToB reports reflect technical reality, not finding-count targets; weakest is code and difficulty, with zero mechanism and the seven brocards themselves adapted from Woodruff's 2026 blog post (properly credited), so the original work is only the operationalization into PASS/DISMISS/NEEDS-MORE-INFO tests.
note_c: The standout is the falsifiable sequential triage framing with explicit PASS, DISMISS, and NEEDS-MORE-INFO outcomes; the weakest is that it is a well-attributed procedural checklist rather than an executable triage system.

name: Grilling
author: Matt Pocock
note_o: Standout is ingenuity by a wide margin — it reframes requirements-gathering as a topological walk of a design tree, where the 'frontier' is exactly the set of decisions whose prerequisites are settled, a question depending on another open question is deferred to a later round by construction, an in-flight fact-finding subagent counts as an unsettled prerequisite so only its downstream blocks, and facts are the agent's job while decisions are the user's; weakest is code and difficulty, since the entire artifact is 1,872 bytes of prose with no mechanism, and it shows the question template but never a filled-in round, so nothing demonstrates the frontier computation on a real problem.
note_c: Standout is ingenuity: treating unresolved decisions as a prerequisite frontier yields a disciplined adaptive interview rather than a flat questionnaire; weakest is code quality because the design-tree behavior is specified but not mechanized.

name: Semgrep Rule Creator
author: Trail of Bits
note_o: Standout is organization plus domain precision: a short SKILL.md router, a syntax-lookup quick-reference, and a procedural workflow.md with no overlap, carrying details only someone who has debugged real rules would write down (annotation must sit on the line immediately before the code with nothing else on it, `$VAR` must be uppercase, Go typed metavariables use `($READER : *zip.Reader)` colon syntax, `semgrep --dataflow-traces` for taint debugging); weakest is code and difficulty — nothing executable ships, and the mandatory step of WebFetching seven external documentation URLs before writing any rule makes the workflow dependent on live third-party links with no stated fallback if one 404s.
note_c: Its standout is a credible static-analysis workflow that couples AST inspection with false-positive tests, while code quality is absent because it includes examples and instructions rather than a working rule or automation.

name: paper-relevance-rank
author: Xin (applicant)
note_o: Standout is product judgment — the user and moment are unmistakable (tier papers against a date-stamped profile of one specific Hyperliquid paper, with hard scope rules: only re-tier named sections, the user's stated tier overrides the model's, never silently delete, demote and explain); weakest is completeness, since every input path points at files not shipped (overleaf/0_abstract.tex, paper_site/new_papers.html, corpus/inventory/paper-locations.md) so nobody but the author can run it end to end.
note_c: The standout is unusually specific product judgment in the five research anchors and comparability breaks; the weakest is the complete absence of an executable artifact behind ranking, discovery, or site reordering.

name: Orca Linear
author: Stably AI
note_o: Standout is ingenuity: deliberately refusing to document any subcommand and instead making the binary serve its own version-matched guide via `ORCA skills get orca-linear` dissolves skill/binary drift rather than managing it, and the resolution ladder that avoids bare `orca` on Linux because it would launch the GNOME screen reader is exactly the detail only shipped experience teaches; weakest is code, as the file contains no artifact beyond a handful of literal command lines.
note_c: Standout: resolving the executable once and loading a version-matched guide is a sharp solution to CLI drift and the Linux GNOME-Orca collision; weakest: the intentionally tiny stub contains no implementation and requires an external binary to supply the actual command contract.

name: Algorithmic Art
author: Anthropic
note_o: Standout is code/web craft — viewer.html is a complete self-contained page with CSS custom properties for the palette, a grid seed-control cluster and a real sidebar layout, pinned p5.js 1.7.0; weakest is organization and ingenuity together, with a 19.7KB monolithic SKILL.md that has no references/ split, a generator_template.js that is comment scaffolding with no working algorithm, and an instruction to repeat phrases like 'meticulously crafted algorithm' and 'painstaking optimization' — self-hype substituted for mechanism.
note_c: The standout is a usable seeded p5 viewer template with coherent layout and controls; the weakest is ingenuity because the prescribed generic philosophy-to-particles recipe supplies no distinctive generative mechanism.

name: Idea Refine
author: Addy Osmani
note_o: Organization and completeness carry it — SKILL.md stays at 8KB with frameworks/criteria/examples each in one file, and examples.md contains full worked sessions with real user turns; difficulty is the weakest, since the only executable artifact is a 12-line bash script that runs mkdir -p docs/ideas and the frameworks (SCAMPER, HMW, JTBD, first principles) are standard-issue with no mechanism behind them.
note_c: Product judgment stands out in making assumptions and a deliberate Not Doing list mandatory before saving an artifact; ingenuity is weakest because the divergent/convergent framework is conventional.

name: linear-tickets
author: Stably AI
note_o: Standout is ingenuity and product judgment in one move — the file deliberately contains no command surface at all ('this file is a discovery stub, not the usage guide') so the docs can never drift from the binary, delegating to `ORCA skills get linear-tickets`, and the executable-resolution ladder catches a genuinely nasty real-world collision (bare `orca` on Linux outside an Orca terminal is the GNOME screen reader and would start speech on the user's machine), with a refusal to fall through to a different binary; weakest is completeness and difficulty, because the actual payload ships in an unavailable binary so a reader without Orca installed gets nothing runnable, and the frontmatter description is a single bloated run-on sentence that fights its own stub-like discipline.
note_c: Standout is ingenuity: resolving the correct CLI once and loading a version-matched guide avoids both command drift and the Linux screen-reader collision; weakest is code quality because the actual integration is delegated to an external binary.

name: Review Animations
author: Emil Kowalski
note_o: Standout is product judgment — `disable-model-invocation: true` plus an explicit refusal to review non-motion code is scope cut on purpose, and the output contract (findings table first, tiered verdict, binary Block/Approve with named blocking conditions) leaves nothing to interpretation; weakest is code, since there is no executable artifact at all — the front-end evidence is judgment (transform-origin, GPU-only properties, recalc storms from parent CSS variables, hover-pointer gating) expressed as prose and cited cubic-beziers.
note_c: Standout product judgment: the frequency-first deletion rule and explicit block criteria make the intended design-review moment unusually concrete; weakest code evidence: it supplies standards and snippets but no executable reviewer or demonstrated review of a real diff.

name: TDD
author: Matt Pocock
note_o: Standout is ingenuity — three sharp non-obvious framings that beat the usual red-green recitation: the tautological test (expected values must come from an independent source, not recomputed the way the code computes them), horizontal slicing versus vertical tracer-bullet slices, and the deliberate revision that refactoring is not part of the loop but belongs to review; weakest is completeness, since it hard-depends on two skills that are not shipped here (/codebase-design for seam vocabulary, code-review for the refactor stage) and on an optional CONTEXT.md whose format is never specified.
note_c: The standout is the explicit seam-agreement and vertical-slice framing, which prevents brittle implementation-coupled tests; the weakest is code quality because its examples are pedagogical snippets rather than a tested executable artifact.

name: Social
author: Corey Haines
note_o: Organization and product lead — a 15KB index routing to eight single-purpose references plus a copy-me listening-sources template, reading .agents/product-marketing.md first so the user isn't re-interrogated, an explicit Do Not Engage list, and 'always ask before posting, output drafts' as a consent default; ingenuity is the weakest, since pillars/hooks/calendar/repurposing tables are standard marketing-playbook material and only the carousel framework-selection table with per-framework failure modes shows an original cut.
note_c: Organization stands out in separating post formats, listening setup, platform limits, and evaluation cases; code is weakest because the social workflow is mostly guidance rather than implemented tooling.

name: AI SEO
author: Corey Haines
note_o: Standout is ingenuity in references/citations-vs-recommendations.md — the retrieved/cited/mentioned/recommended ladder plus the 'shadow rung' (recommended against) and the finding that 69% of self-promotional listicle citations route buyers to competitors is a genuinely counterintuitive, sourced reframing; weakest is code/difficulty, since all 75KB is markdown plus an evals.json assertion list with no mechanism that executes anything.
note_c: Organization stands out through separated references and eval cases, while code is weakest because the seven-file skill provides no executable audit or optimization mechanism.

name: Obsidian Bases
author: Steph Ango (kepano)
note_o: Standout is organization and completeness — a clean two-file split (entry doc plus FUNCTIONS_REFERENCE.md) with three fully copy-pasteable working bases and a troubleshooting section built from wrong/correct pairs, including the non-obvious Duration trap that .days must be accessed before .round(); weakest is ingenuity and code, since this is a faithful DSL reference with no executable artifact, and the map view is left a stub ('Map-specific settings for lat/lng properties') while every other view type is fully specified.
note_c: The standout is practical product judgment around YAML quoting, duration semantics, and complete Base examples; the weakest is that the skill offers documentation only, with no validator or other executable support.

name: Pricing Strategy
author: Corey Haines
note_o: Standout is the second teardown axis -- scoring a pricing page for AI-agent readability (price in HTML text vs image/JS-only/PDF, per-tier limits stated in words, Product/Offer JSON-LD, AI search bots unblocked in robots.txt) with a '30-second paste test' that is honestly labelled a heuristic rather than proof, credited to Kyle Poyar, and handed off to the sibling `schema` and `ai-seo` skills; weakest is code/difficulty, since evals/evals.json defines prompts, expected_output and per-case assertions but ships no runner to execute them, and the rest is domain prose in three reference files.
note_c: Product judgment stands out in the intentionally scoped two-axis pricing-page teardown, including human buyer clarity and AI extractability; code is weakest because the substantial research and evaluation material contains no executable artifact.

name: paper-regression-writeup
author: Xin (applicant)
note_o: Standout is product judgment plus the ingenuity of two opinionated inversions — 'a table of coefficients with no equation is a failure' (infer and mark the equation when the paper omits it) and the intraday-collapse rule that pins one row = one position-day — all carried by a real worked example with live numbers from Aquilina et al. Table 5; weakest is code, as the file is pure prose with a single stray CSS declaration and no runnable artifact.
note_c: Ingenuity stands out in the bidirectional equation-to-results rule and explicit intraday-collapse treatment, while code is weakest because the dossier ships only prose guidance.

name: source-role
author: Xin (applicant)
note_o: Standout is product judgment plus the ingenuity of the design — warehouse-first retrieval with external capture as an explicitly budgeted fallback whose catch always sinks back into the warehouse (the flywheel), a second judgment axis nobody usually encodes ('is this person actually poachable from their current company tier, and why would they move'), a credit ceiling that prints 'still short X, spent about Y' instead of faking completion, and a stated when-NOT-to-run for filled or non-starving roles; weakest is completeness and organization, because the entire mechanism (`src/fit.py`, `src/ingest.py`, `push_pipeline`, `config/weights.json`, `judgment_rubric.md`, the Monday board id 5028513251 and column `long_text_mm4dzdfj`) is assumed present but never shipped, and all seven stages plus the embedded Python snippet live in one undivided 8KB file.
note_c: Standout is product judgment: warehouse-first sourcing, credit limits, and human-review gates show unusually clear operational priorities; weakest is completeness because all fit, ingestion, push, and sync mechanisms are only referenced, not included.

name: Git Guardrails for Claude Code
author: Matt Pocock
note_o: Standout is product judgment — it asks install scope first, offers pattern customization, warns to merge rather than overwrite an existing hooks.PreToolUse array, and ends with an exact echo-pipe verification command and expected exit code 2; weakest is ingenuity, since the mechanism is an unanchored substring `grep -qE` over nine literals that both false-positives on `echo "git push"` and misses trivial spacing variants, with jq assumed present and unchecked.
note_c: Standout product judgment: it asks for project versus global scope and preserves existing settings; weakest code quality: the jq-dependent substring regex hook misses command variants and can overmatch unrelated shell text.

name: Requesting Code Review
author: Jesse Vincent (obra)
note_o: Standout is ingenuity — the framing that review is context hygiene rather than quality theater (hand the reviewer precisely crafted context, never session history, so the diff and the evaluation live in the subagent's window and only findings come back), plus the read-only discipline of `git worktree add /tmp/review-[SHA]` instead of ever moving HEAD on the working checkout; weakest is code and difficulty, since the deliverable is one prompt template with four placeholders and a severity rubric.
note_c: The standout is the tightly scoped, read-only reviewer handoff with severity calibration and concrete output requirements; the weakest is code quality because it supplies orchestration instructions and a prompt template, not runnable review machinery.

name: academic-writing-finance
author: Xin (applicant)
note_o: Standout is organization (a 6KB SKILL.md routing to four single-purpose reference files — rubric, two canon lists, shadowing protocol — with no duplication) and the ingenuity of the drills (the inversion exercise that writes the bad version as a measuring instrument, the word-counted paragraph label map, and the explicit 'separate what is imitable from what depends on the author's seniority'); weakest is code, since there is no executable artifact anywhere in the five files, and completeness suffers because the promised accumulating references/distilled-rules.md is never shipped and no worked analysis of a real passage is included.
note_c: Standout is product judgment: the architecture-map, shadowing, and draft-diagnosis modes target a very specific finance researcher; weakest is code quality because the dossier ships only prose and reference material.

name: Audit Augmentation
author: Trail of Bits
note_o: Standout is product judgment: When NOT to Use, the mandatory preanalysis-before-augment ordering, and the explicit hand-off to trailmark-finding-triage make the moment of use unmistakable; weakest is code, since the file ships no executable artifact — the SARIF/weAudit line-overlap matching it describes lives inside trailmark, and the only original logic here is a four-line hasattr version gate.
note_c: Standout: it gives a concrete audit-triage workflow around line-overlap matching, unmatched findings, and pre-analysis context; weakest: all substantive graph augmentation is delegated to Trailmark, with no executable implementation in the submitted files.

name: SEO Audit
author: Corey Haines
note_o: Standout is ingenuity: the schema-detection limitation section catches a tool-aware failure the checklist genre normally misses — web_fetch strips <script> tags so JS-injected JSON-LD is invisible, making "no schema found" a false finding — and evals.json turns that into a testable assertion; weakest is code, since the skill is a 16KB checklist plus two reference documents with no executable artifact and no mechanism that would make a strong engineer pause.
note_c: The schema-detection limitation and test assertions show the strongest judgment, while code quality is absent because the audit is implemented as extensive procedural guidance rather than executable inspection tooling.

name: paper-reading-site-summary
author: Xin (applicant)
note_o: Standout is ingenuity/product — it pins one canonical comparison baseline with its actual equations and sign conventions (markout M_{i,h}=s_i(m_{t+h}-p̄_i)q_i decomposed into T_{i,h}+EC_i) so every paper page is forced onto the same metric definition, and it bans the specific silent error of equating a markout with a round-trip return, plus a literal BAD/GOOD prose pair; weakest is code and completeness — nothing executable ships, and the finish step depends on `paper_site/build.sh` and factsheets that live outside the skill with no sample JSON output included.
note_c: The strongest evidence is the unusually precise same-concept metric comparison guardrail; the weakest is the lack of executable extraction, JSON validation, or build mechanism.

name: Competitor Profiling
author: Corey Haines
note_o: Standout is product judgment — quick-scan vs deep-profile cost tiers, a default of prioritizing five over profiling twelve, an eval file asserting the model recommends updating an existing profile rather than restarting, and a legacy-filename fallback for product-marketing.md showing a second pass; weakest is code and completeness, since there is no executable artifact at all and every step depends on two paid MCP servers (Firecrawl, DataForSEO) with no install path and only placeholder outputs, never a real profile.
note_c: The standout is the deliberate dated raw-data snapshot structure that makes competitive claims auditable; the weakest is that all scraping, integration, persistence, and synthesis behavior is only described rather than implemented.

name: Ponytail
author: Dietrich Gebert
note_o: Standout is ingenuity: the seven-rung ladder with "stop at the first rung that holds" plus the `ponytail:` comment convention that makes a deliberate corner-cut self-documenting and greppable ("# ponytail: global lock, per-account locks if throughput matters") is a genuinely stealable idea, reinforced by the counter-rule that laziness never shortens comprehension; weakest is code, as the whole skill is a single 6KB behavioral SKILL.md with no executable artifact.
note_c: Its standout is the concrete decision ladder that combines YAGNI with caller tracing and bounded self-checks, while code quality is necessarily weakest because it supplies no executable implementation.

name: Test-Driven Development
author: Jesse Vincent (obra)
note_o: Standout is ingenuity: writing-good-tests.md's Gate Function forces you to name the production change that would make the test fail before writing the body, and derives from it three sharp disqualifiers — the mirror assertion where the same builder computes both sides, the change detector that only intentional decisions can break, and the rule that documents instructing agents are tested by the consuming agent's behavior while prose for humans earns no test at all; weakest is code and completeness — both files are prose with illustrative TypeScript, the run command is a generic `npm test path/to/test.test.ts` with no stated framework or prerequisites, and no runnable artifact demonstrates the cycle end to end.
note_c: Its standout is the unusually concrete test-quality heuristic of naming the production change a test should catch, while code quality is absent because both files are prose guidance rather than executable artifacts.

name: er-pass-email
author: Xin (applicant)
note_o: Product judgment is the standout — a named user (EASY Residency DO), a deliberate never-send/draft-only boundary, stage-tiered length, and documented revisions from a real session ('removed all references to inexperience, reframed as category requirements'); code is the weakest at zero executable artifact, four markdown files with the sanitization rules restated in both SKILL.md step 3 and the style guide.
note_c: Product judgment stands out through stage-tiered, human-reviewed drafts and explicit sanitization; code is weakest because the shipped mechanism is prose only.

name: explore-research-repo
author: Xin (applicant)
note_o: Standout is product judgment — the user and moment are unmistakable (a researcher about to meet a repo's author), with a consent gate before cloning and an explicit 'don't embarrass yourself' list; weakest is code, since the entire 12KB skill is a single prose SKILL.md with no executable artifact and only a description of the HTML it wants an agent to emit.
note_c: Product judgment stands out in its author-first reading path and meeting-prep deliverable, while code is weakest because the single SKILL.md contains no executable artifact.

name: paper-reading-critique
author: Xin (applicant)
note_o: Standout is ingenuity: the blind-review inversion ("Read only the supplied summary. Do not open the source PDF") reframes the task as testing a summary's self-sufficiency rather than fact-checking it, and the must-check list encodes hard-won personal failure modes (unit of observation, shared-vs-varying variables, STATED/INFERRED/ASSUMED marking); weakest is code, since the only files are an 8KB prose SKILL.md and a 225-byte openai.yaml with no executable artifact.
note_c: Product judgment stands out in the unusually specific finance-PhD reproducibility checks, while code quality is weakest because the two-file skill contains no executable artifact.

name: portfolio-pass
author: Xin (applicant)
note_o: Standout is product judgment plus one real epistemic insight — 'signals can measure might-need, never wants, so every Suggested ask must be open-ended', the red/yellow/green tiering that forbids manufacturing problems for healthy projects, and the anchor-repair loop encoding a real past failure (the Ethena X handle); weakest is code/completeness, because fetch_public_signals.py, gtm_gap_rules.md G1-G9 and budget.guard('dune') are all referenced and none are shipped.
