note_c: Standout product judgment is the disciplined distinction between observable public signals and inferred needs with explicit budget and review limits; weakest completeness is that the collection scripts, rules, configs, and artifact implementation are absent.

name: obsidian-markdown
author: Steph Ango (kepano)
note_o: Standout is organization — a 5KB entry doc that hands off to three focused references (CALLOUTS/EMBEDS/PROPERTIES) with no duplication or orphans, exactly the progressive-disclosure shape the rubric describes, reinforced by a hard scope cut ('covers only Obsidian-specific extensions; standard Markdown is assumed knowledge') and a stated decision rule for wikilinks vs Markdown links; weakest is code/difficulty, since it is a syntax cheatsheet for an already-documented format with zero executable artifact.
note_c: Standout organization is the compact entry guide with distinct callout, embed, and property references plus a full worked note; weakest code quality is that it documents syntax without executable validation or tooling.

name: Verification Before Completion
author: Jesse Vincent (obra)
note_o: Standout is product judgment at 3.6KB — a claim/requires/not-sufficient table plus a rationalization-prevention table that pre-empts the exact excuses a model generates ('I'm confident', 'just this once', 'different words so the rule doesn't apply'), and the red-green revert cycle as the only proof a regression test works; weakest is difficulty, as there is no mechanism at all, only a discipline rule the model is asked to self-enforce.
note_c: Product judgment stands out in its concrete claim-to-verification gate and anti-rationalization table, while difficulty is weakest because it is a short procedural rule without an automation mechanism.

name: gtm-serve
author: Xin (applicant)
note_o: Standout is product judgment — the thesis that a cold list is raw material and the warm-intro path is the deliverable, backed by concrete Monday board IDs (5028598934, 5029746903), a 15-target default, an Apollo credit-guard that only spends reveal() on human-approved targets, a path-owner-consent field, and an explicit 'when not to use this' section; weakest is completeness, since every mechanism it depends on (src/apollo.py, src/gtm_match.py, src/push_gtm.py, config/monday_boards.json) lives outside the skill and no worked input/output is shown.
note_c: The standout is product judgment: it makes warm-intro ownership, consent, review, and credit limits first-class; the weakest is reproducibility because every referenced script and config file is absent from the one-file inventory.

name: paper-coread-update
author: Xin (applicant)
note_o: Standout is ingenuity: the close-the-loop rule (2+ questions of the same shape trigger distill-preferences to push the pattern into paper-coread/references/question-guide.md so future pre-reads pre-empt it) plus the reframe that an already-answered question means the page's navigation failed, not that it needs another Q&A box; weakest is code/completeness, since the file ships no executable artifact and its mechanics (cap of 8, `N Q` TOC tags, ANSWERED/PARTIAL/OPEN statuses) reference a template and sibling skill that are not in this directory.
note_c: Its standout is product judgment: the first-read triage rule, caps, and displacement policy make a specific reader’s co-read page stay useful; its weakest is code quality because SKILL.md contains no executable artifact.

name: paper-reading-summary
author: Xin (applicant)
note_o: Ingenuity is the standout — the Stage 1 orientation / Stage 2 replication-grade split, 'restate the unit of observation and N for each regression table separately', and walking a nested regression ladder column-by-column (-3.12% univariate to +0.14% with trader FE means between-trader selection) are genuinely non-obvious moves; organization is the weakest, a single 20.8KB monolithic SKILL.md with three separable standards (performance-measure, explicit-equation, conclusion-writing) inlined and no references/ split.
note_c: Ingenuity stands out in its unusually precise standards for observation units, conditional coefficients, and reconstruction from raw fields; code is weakest because none is shipped.

name: browser-testing-with-devtools
author: Addy Osmani
note_o: Standout is the security-boundaries section, which is the only part carrying real thought — it reasons about blast radius per connection flag (`--isolated` vs `--autoConnect` vs `--browser-url`, noting Chrome requires a non-default user data dir to open the debugging port), declares all DOM/console/network output untrusted data, and tells the agent to surface 'I can see your open tabs' as a finding rather than a convenience; weakest is organization and code, since 14.5KB of separable material (setup, security doctrine, three ASCII workflows, test-plan template, a11y checklist, rationalizations table) sits in a single monolithic SKILL.md with no scripts and no reference splitting, and the workflow trees are generic debugging advice any engineer would produce unaided.
note_c: Standout is product judgment: the isolated-profile default and explicit untrusted-browser-data boundary address the real danger of authenticated browser automation; weakest is code quality because this is a procedural guide with no executable artifact.

name: Frontend Design
author: Anthropic
note_o: Standout is ingenuity — naming the three specific looks AI design collapses into (cream #F4F1EA + high-contrast serif + terracotta; near-black + acid green; broadsheet hairline rules at zero radius) and then prescribing a self-check where you run a similar prompt to see whether you land in the same place is a genuinely stealable anti-genericness test; weakest is code, with zero snippets — even the one real technical warning (CSS specificity collisions between .section and .cta padding) is stated in prose only.
note_c: The standout is the deliberate anti-template design-planning and self-critique loop; the weakest is code evidence because the skill contains no implementation artifact from which frontend craft can be verified.

name: Receiving Code Review
author: Jesse Vincent (obra)
note_o: Product judgment is the standout — it identifies one narrow failure moment (an agent receiving PR feedback), refuses to grow into a general review skill, and handles the awkward paths a real person hits (you pushed back and were wrong; you can't verify without X; you're uncomfortable pushing back), with the sharp observation that partial understanding of items 1-6 means clarify all before implementing any; code and difficulty are the weakest, a 6KB prose file whose only executable content is one gh api replies URL.
note_c: Product judgment stands out in targeting the exact moment review feedback becomes costly and requiring verification before action; code is weakest because no executable artifact is included.

name: research-intelligence
author: Xin (applicant)
note_o: Standout is ingenuity — the seven-state evidence taxonomy (corroborated/primary-reported/secondary-consensus/single-source/speculative/disputed/stale) plus the rule that repeated syndication adds no source diversity is a real epistemic layer, not boilerplate; weakest is completeness, because every command routes through an unshipped `/Users/xin/Stanford/Research/News Feed/.venv/bin/newsctl` with no worked example, so nothing here runs in a stranger's hands.
note_c: Standout organization: a short entry point cleanly separates evidence semantics, promotion rules, and command lookup; weakest code evidence: every substantive operation is delegated to an unshipped machine-specific newsctl binary.

name: surf
author: Xin (applicant)
note_o: Standout is product judgment — the vendoring header names the upstream commit (asksurf-ai/surf-skills @4d157d19) and enumerates each firm-policy removal to reapply on sync (no CLAUDE.md injection, no feedback upload of chat turns, no per-session self-update), and the Gotchas are real field findings (hyperliquid-fills must walk meta.next_cursor ascending or you silently sum PnL from a ~2000-fill window; volume_usd always returns 0); weakest is code, as this is a 20k single-file CLI usage guide with no executable artifact and most of its bulk inherited from upstream.
note_c: Standout is the unusually concrete endpoint-routing guidance, especially token resolution and cursor-safe fill history; weakest is that the skill is a monolithic, explicitly vendored CLI manual with no implementation artifact.

name: Ads
author: Corey Haines
note_o: Standout is product judgment — the intent-routing table forces the relevant playbook to load before any live-account kill/scale decision ('the thresholds live there, not here') and the 2026 Andromeda reframe is stated as directional with a named test to run, while evals/evals.json encodes per-prompt assertions; weakest is code and difficulty — 110KB of pure markdown with no mechanism, and copy formulas are duplicated between the 25KB SKILL.md and references/ad-copy-templates.md.
note_c: Progressive routing to decision-specific playbooks is strong organizational product work; the claimed direct account access has no connector or operational mechanism in the files.

name: Animation Vocabulary
author: Emil Kowalski
note_o: Standout is product judgment and the reverse-lookup framing — the skill inverts the usual 'how do I build this animation' tool into 'what is this effect called so you can ask for it', states the non-goal explicitly ('for naming an effect, not designing or building one'), fixes the output format, and forbids inventing terms outside the glossary; weakest is code/difficulty, as it is a 13KB curated glossary with no executable artifact and no mechanism a strong engineer would stall on.
note_c: Standout product judgment is the tightly scoped reverse lookup and concise disambiguation format; weakest code quality is that the submission is only a glossary and instructions with no executable artifact.

name: JSON Canvas
author: Steph Ango (kepano)
note_o: Standout is product judgment: the four workflows map exactly onto what an agent actually does to a .canvas file, and suggested widths/heights plus 50-100px spacing mean the common case needs zero decisions from the user; weakest is code, since there is no executable artifact at all — the validation checklist is prose the model must perform by hand rather than a validator, on a spec the author already owns.
note_c: Standout: it is a well-structured schema guide with concrete validation invariants and useful complete canvas examples; weakest: it provides no parser, ID generator, collision handling, or layout algorithm beyond manual instructions.

name: Cavecrew
author: Julius Brussee
note_o: Standout is ingenuity: it reframes subagent choice as context economics rather than capability (tool results are injected into main context verbatim, so a compressed ~700-token investigator return beats a 2k-token vanilla Explore across 20 delegations) and specifies each agent's return as a parseable contract with terminal first tokens (`too-big.` / `needs-confirm.`) and grep-safe `path:\d+`, with an auto-clarity carve-out dropping compression for security warnings and irreversible-action confirmations; weakest is completeness/difficulty, as the three agents it routes to are not in this directory and the skill itself is a 3.9KB decision table with no mechanism a strong engineer would have to stop and think about.
note_c: Ingenuity stands out in treating compressed, machine-greppable subagent output as a context-budget product constraint; code is weakest because the promised presets and compression mechanism are not included.

name: Vercel Composition Patterns
author: Vercel Labs
note_o: Product is the relative standout — the state/actions/meta context contract with two swappable providers (local ForwardMessageProvider vs global ChannelProvider) is a genuinely usable API opinion, and the React 19 section is gated behind an explicit version warning; organization is weakest, with the same Composer example restated verbatim across SKILL.md, README.md, AGENTS.md and rules/, and AGENTS.md labelled 'Compiled output (generated)' while no generator is shipped.
note_c: The standout is clear rule-level organization with useful React examples, while the weakest is ingenuity because the advice is conventional composition guidance and the compiled AGENTS.md duplicates the rule corpus.

name: Doc Co-Authoring
author: Anthropic
note_o: Standout is product judgment — every real branch is handled (artifacts vs plain file, integrations present vs absent, user answers with numbers vs freeform, images lacking alt-text so a later Claude can't read the doc), plus a stated exit condition for context gathering and a str_replace-never-reprint editing discipline; weakest is code, since there is no executable artifact at all, and Stage 3's clever fresh-sub-agent reader test is described only as instructions with no harness.
note_c: Standout is the fresh-reader testing loop, which directly targets author-context blind spots; weakest is the long monolithic workflow's reliance on unspecified artifacts, integrations, and sub-agent capabilities.

name: Copywriting
author: Corey Haines
note_o: Standout is product judgment: it reads .agents/product-marketing.md before interrogating the user (including the legacy filename, evidence of a second pass) and routes explicitly to copy-editing/cro/emails instead of absorbing them; weakest is difficulty, since the substance is a curated compendium of standard headline formulas and section templates with no mechanism a strong engineer would pause over.
note_c: Standout: the page-purpose context gate, anti-fabrication rule, and eval assertions show a clear conversion-writing workflow; weakest: it is conventional prose guidance with no executable artifact or demonstrated generated output.

name: er-brief
author: Xin (applicant)
note_o: Standout is product judgment — a named moment of use (night before IC), scope deliberately cut ('max 3 core questions, only ones the call can uniquely resolve', no SWOT) and a real unhappy path encoded (the FinTax memo with pasted sections from another company must be flagged, not smoothed over); weakest is code/completeness, since there is no executable artifact at all and the two files it routes to (`../_shared/monday-conventions.md`, `../_shared/output-samples/bad-examples.md`) are outside the skill and unshipped.
note_c: Product judgment stands out in the provenance-first, three-question brief constraint; code is absent, with Monday and Drive retrieval only described.

name: talent-pass
author: Xin (applicant)
note_o: Standout is product judgment: the top banner retires the skill's original blind-scan discovery with a stated reason (the library drifted from actual hiring demand and burned credit) and reroutes to /source-role, plus real observed-failure rules like overriding GitHub's `company` field when it holds an alma mater or a joke ('Block 6.282e+10') because stale values skew the source-prestige score; weakest is organization, since one file now carries both a deprecated path and the live one, step 6 is an empty 'merged into 2b' stub, and none of the referenced src/*.py or data/*.json ships with it.
note_c: Product judgment stands out in the deliberate shift from indiscriminate discovery to role-led maintenance and explicit incomplete-record handling; code is weakest because the referenced discovery, enrichment, scoring, and sync implementations are not shipped.

name: Emil Design Eng
author: Emil Kowalski
note_o: Ingenuity is the standout — leading with a frequency table that says 100+/day actions get no animation ever (Raycast has none) inverts the usual animation guide, and 'never animate from scale(0), nothing in the real world appears from nothing' is a memorable reframe backed by real CSS (transform-origin: var(--transform-origin), transitions over keyframes for interruptibility); organization is the weakest, a single 27KB file with no progressive disclosure and a mandated first response that plugs the author's paid course.
note_c: Product judgment stands out in frequency-sensitive animation guidance and concrete interaction exceptions; organization is weakest because all guidance lives in one long monolith.

name: Incremental Implementation
author: Addy Osmani
note_o: Standout is product framing — a clear when-to/when-NOT-to gate (skip for single-file changes), a concrete script for directing an agent per increment, and the agent-specific 'don't re-run the same build command with no intervening edit' rule; weakest is completeness, since the closing See Also points at references/definition-of-done.md and two sibling skills that are not shipped, and the TypeScript is illustrative only (a feature-flag const, an options?.notify ?? false default), so the content is textbook vertical-slicing doctrine with no mechanism.
note_c: Standout product judgment is the risk-first and rollback-friendly slicing discipline with a prohibition on redundant verification; weakest code quality is that examples illustrate policy but no implementation enforces it.

name: deal-pass
author: Xin (applicant)
note_o: Standout is ingenuity: the new-track bootstrap distills founder patterns against a ~6-person non-founder control group and explicitly discards features the control group also has, then gates the pipeline on eval_deal.py AUC >= 0.75 and closes the loop by re-weighting patterns from investor feedback; weakest is completeness/code, since the skill dir holds only SKILL.md and every mechanism (discover_deal.py, score_deal.py, config/founder_dna.json, .env) lives outside it, so nothing here is runnable or verifiable by a stranger.
note_c: Product judgment stands out in the explicit early-founder, contact-gated, budget-aware funnel; code is weakest because every claimed pipeline command and scoring mechanism is absent from the shipped file.

name: Pick UI Library
author: Emil Kowalski
note_o: Standout is product judgment: 'disable-model-invocation: true' plus 'recommend one library, don't present a menu' plus 'check package.json first; if it uses a competitor, flag it but don't churn the dependency' are three deliberate scope cuts, and the 'Common mismatches' section indexes by the anti-pattern the agent will actually encounter rather than by library name; weakest is code and difficulty — it is a 4.5KB lookup table with no mechanism and nothing a strong engineer would stop and think about.
note_c: Standout product judgment: it gives one opinionated default while preserving already-installed dependencies and avoids needless churn; weakest code quality: it is a curated prose lookup with no executable artifact.

name: Content Strategy
author: Corey Haines
note_o: Standout is organization — genuine progressive disclosure across SKILL.md, references/headless-cms.md and evals/evals.json, plus a revised opinion left visible ('most content works fine under /blog; only use hub/spoke URLs for major topics'), and an eval file with per-prompt assertions is unusually disciplined for a prose skill; weakest is difficulty/ingenuity, since the substance is standard content-marketing doctrine (pillars, hub-and-spoke, buyer-stage modifiers, weighted scoring) with no mechanism behind it.
note_c: Standout organization is the short operational guide separated from CMS reference material and concrete evaluation cases; weakest code quality is that no executable implementation accompanies the strategy framework.

name: supply-chain-risk-auditor
author: Trail of Bits
note_o: Standout is product judgment — tight When/When NOT to use boundaries that route active scanning to npm audit and pip-audit, a prerequisite check for gh, insistence that every cited star/issue count come from a real query, and an explicit ban on 'opposite' columns so absence from the report is itself the low-risk signal; weakest is completeness and difficulty, since 'Finding all git repositories for direct dependencies' is one unexplained line covering the actual hard work across every package ecosystem, and no worked example with real input or output is shipped.
note_c: The standout is a focused risk taxonomy paired with a concise report template and replacement recommendation step; the weakest is that dependency discovery and evidence collection are left entirely to prose instructions.

name: Code Review and Quality
author: Addy Osmani
note_o: Standout is product judgment in the finding-severity taxonomy (Critical/Nit/Optional/FYI with author action, plus 'if you have one structural problem and ten nits, the structural problem is the review'); weakest is organization and originality — one monolithic 20KB entry doc with no progressive disclosure, and the approval standard, ~100/300/1000-line sizing, splitting-strategy table and one-business-day rule are lifted from Google's eng-practices code review guide with no attribution.
note_c: Product judgment stands out in prioritizing high-leverage structural findings and named remedies, while code is weakest because this is a monolithic review checklist without executable tooling.

name: copy-editing
author: Corey Haines
note_o: Standout is product judgment — an exhaustive trigger-phrase description, a context handshake that reads .agents/product-marketing.md with named legacy-filename fallbacks, and an Always/Recommended/Optional/Skip tier telling the reader when the expensive expert-panel pass is not worth running; weakest is code and difficulty, since there is no executable artifact at all and the seven sweeps plus the Plain English word tables are a checklist rendered as a skill.
note_c: The standout is its organized seven-pass editorial workflow with evaluation prompts and focused reference material; the weakest is technical complexity because it is entirely prose guidance with no executable mechanism.

name: Dispatching Parallel Agents
author: Jesse Vincent (obra)
note_o: Standout is product judgment — it is short, has a concrete when-NOT-to-use list (related failures, shared state, exploratory debugging), a full worked prompt, and a real logged session with actual test filenames and what each agent found, which reads as lived rather than invented; weakest is ingenuity and difficulty, because 'one agent per independent domain' is now the obvious approach and the single operationally non-obvious fact in the whole file is 'multiple dispatch calls in one response = parallel, one per response = sequential', with the graphviz digraph shipped as an unrendered source block that adds nothing a two-line rule would not.
note_c: Standout is organization: the independence decision tree, scoped-prompt pattern, and integration check make the workflow easy to navigate; weakest is code quality because the skill contains no implementation of dispatch or coordination.

name: Obsidian CLI
author: Steph Ango (kepano)
note_o: Product judgment is the standout — it refuses to enumerate the command list ('Run `obsidian help`... This is always up to date') and instead encodes only the two things an agent gets wrong, the parameters-take-`=` vs bare-flags syntax model and the reload/dev:errors/screenshot plugin loop; code is weakest, as there is no artifact at all beyond bash one-liners invoking someone else's binary.
note_c: The standout is a concise, specific command reference for a running Obsidian user, while the weakest is code quality because it is documentation over an existing CLI with no executable artifact of its own.

name: Test-Driven Development
author: Addy Osmani
note_o: Standout is the 'Discover the Stack First' section, which names the actual agent failure mode (assuming npm test) and routes every RED/GREEN step through checked-in wrappers like ./gradlew or make test; weakest is organization and originality — 16KB in one file with no progressive disclosure, and the substance of the test-size taxonomy, DAMP-over-DRY, state-not-interactions and the named 'Beyonce Rule' is Google's testing canon reproduced with no attribution.
note_c: Standout product judgment: stack discovery before RED/GREEN and the prove-it pattern address common cross-repository agent mistakes; weakest code quality: all implementation is generic example code rather than a runnable testing tool.

name: Writing Plans
author: Jesse Vincent (obra)
note_o: Standout is ingenuity — the format's non-obvious rules all derive from one coherent premise, that each task is executed by a fresh subagent seeing only its own task: hence the mandatory Consumes/Produces interface block with exact signatures, the ban on "Similar to Task N" because tasks get read out of order, and task right-sizing defined as the boundary where a reviewer could reject one task while approving its neighbor; weakest is completeness, since execution depends on three unshipped sibling skills (subagent-driven-development, executing-plans, using-git-worktrees) and no filled-in plan is ever shown end to end.
note_c: Standout product judgment: per-task interfaces and independently testable review gates anticipate handoff failures; weakest code evidence: the artifact is a prescriptive planning checklist with no executable mechanism.

name: distill-preferences
author: Xin (applicant)
note_o: Standout is product judgment — the routing rule sends each preference to exactly ONE most-upstream home and the closing report exists so the user can veto a misread, an unhappy path a real person hits; weakest is code/difficulty, since the entire skill is a 2.6KB SKILL.md with no executable artifact and no mechanism enforcing 'never create a duplicate'.
note_c: The standout is product judgment in routing each durable preference to one upstream home, while the weakest is code because the skill contains no executable mechanism.

name: Scaffold Exercises
author: Matt Pocock
note_o: Standout is completeness/product for its size — a real worked example goes from a three-line plan to the exact mkdir -p commands and the exact readme stub paths, with a chosen default ('default to explainer/ unless the plan specifies otherwise') and git mv over mv to preserve history; weakest is difficulty, since the whole skill is mkdir plus a lint-and-iterate loop against `pnpm ai-hero-cli internal lint`, a private CLI a stranger cannot run.
note_c: Standout product judgment: it encodes the target repository's numbering, variant, lint, and git-history conventions into a narrow workflow; weakest code quality: the shell commands are examples, not a shipped scaffold command or validator.

name: gtm-match
author: Xin (applicant)
note_o: Standout is product judgment — a named user (YZi BD), a quarterly cadence, a human-review gate before any intro, a match_history.json that downweights previously-rejected pairs, and an explicit 'when not to use' section; weakest is completeness/code, since the only shipped file is prose that invokes src/push_gtm.py, config/monday_boards.json and data/gtm/ paths that are not in the skill at all.
note_c: Standout product judgment is the ordered offer-to-need matching with human-reviewed warm introductions; weakest completeness is that the referenced Monday config, push script, and data files are not shipped.

name: Debugging and Error Recovery
author: Addy Osmani
note_o: Standout is ingenuity within a conventional doc — 'Treating Error Output as Untrusted Data' (stack traces and CI logs as data, never instructions) is a genuinely uncommon inclusion, as is the rationalizations table with a calibrated counter ('you might be right 70% of the time'); weakest is code/difficulty, since nothing executes and the shipped commands are illustrative npm invocations the text itself tells you to substitute.
note_c: Standout product judgment: the ordered reproduce-localize-reduce-fix-guard flow and untrusted-error rule target real agent failure modes; weakest code quality: the TypeScript is illustrative snippets rather than a runnable artifact.

name: handoff
author: Matt Pocock
note_o: Standout is product judgment per byte: 879 bytes carry four deliberate decisions -- write to the OS temp dir not the workspace so handoffs never pollute the repo, reference specs/plans/ADRs/diffs by path instead of duplicating them (so the doc cannot rot against them), emit a 'suggested skills' section to route the next agent, and set `disable-model-invocation: true` with a matching `allow_implicit_invocation: false` in agents/openai.yaml; weakest is difficulty, as it is pure prompt text with no mechanism, no example handoff, and nothing a strong engineer would need to reproduce.
note_c: Product judgment stands out in avoiding duplicate artifacts and requiring sensitive-data redaction during a session transition; code is weakest because no executable handoff or validation mechanism is provided.

name: paper-reading-methodology
author: Xin (applicant)
note_o: Standout is product judgment — a specific reader (empirical finance researcher) at a specific moment, with domain-earned rules like distinguishing dollar volume vs dollar value vs portfolio value and 'if the paper states a definition in words, write the implied equation anyway and label it a reconstruction from prose'; weakest is code/completeness, since the entire skill is one 11.7k prose SKILL.md with no executable artifact, no worked example, and a closing prompt template that restates the body verbatim.
note_c: Standout is the explicit general-model-to-paper mapping and reproducibility checklist for a clearly imagined researcher; weakest is that it is a single prose prompt with no executable mechanism or shipped research tooling.

name: paper-reading-repair
author: Xin (applicant)
note_o: Standout is product judgment: scope is cut hard and deliberately (edit only the named summary JSON, preserve id and top-level schema, log unresolvable points into `corrections` rather than guessing), with one sharp rule worth stealing -- a same-concept mapping must be justified from the source metric's formula, sign, reference anchor, and horizon, never from similar terminology; weakest is code/difficulty, as the entire skill is 1,366 bytes of prose plus a 206-byte openai.yaml with no executable artifact, no schema definition, and no worked example of a critique-to-repair pass.
note_c: Product judgment is strongest in preserving schema and identifiers while forcing source-grounded corrections; code is weakest because the artifact is purely procedural prose.

name: Internal Comms
author: Anthropic
note_o: Standout is organization — a 1.5KB entry doc that does nothing but classify the request and route to one of four examples/*.md guideline files, with general-comms.md as the explicit catch-all and no duplicated instructions; weakest is difficulty and code, since the whole artifact is four prose format templates (the 3P one is literally three labeled lines plus an emoji) with no mechanism whatsoever behind the Slack/Drive/Email gathering it asks for.
note_c: The standout is progressive disclosure into concise, purpose-specific communication formats with realistic information-gathering guidance; the weakest is ingenuity because the underlying routing-and-template approach is conventional.

name: Shipping and Launch
author: Addy Osmani
note_o: Standout is the rollout decision threshold table, which replaces the usual 'monitor after deploy' hand-wave with numbers you can act on (advance if error rate is within 10% of baseline and P95 within 20%, roll back at >2x baseline or >50% latency, new client JS errors above 0.1% of sessions); weakest is completeness and organization -- the 'See Also' block points at references/definition-of-done.md, security-checklist.md, performance-checklist.md and accessibility-checklist.md, none of which exist in this single-file skill, so four of its promised deliverables are dangling.
note_c: Product judgment stands out in explicit rollout thresholds, rollback triggers, and feature-flag lifecycle rules; code is weakest because the React and server snippets are illustrative rather than a runnable launch mechanism.

name: Design Taste Frontend v1
author: Leon (Leonxlnx)
note_o: Standout is the quantified-taste framing — three numeric dials (DESIGN_VARIANCE 8, MOTION_INTENSITY 6, VISUAL_DENSITY 4) that later sections actually branch on ('centered heroes banned when DESIGN_VARIANCE > 4'), backed by real production knowledge (min-h-[100dvh] over h-screen for iOS Safari, useMotionValue/useTransform instead of useState for magnetic hover, staggerChildren parent and children must share one client-component tree); weakest is organization, a 21KB single-file monolith of ALL-CAPS BANNED/MANDATORY directives with no references split, no examples, and no failure modes, submitted as the explicitly-deprecated v1.
note_c: Standout ingenuity is the three-dial design system that maps variance, motion, and density to concrete implementation constraints; weakest completeness is the lack of a runnable example or shipped components proving the extensive directives cohere.

name: paper-reading-factsheet
author: Xin (applicant)
note_o: Standout is product judgment — the scope is cut hard to one artifact (`summaries/factsheets/<Authors_Year>.md`) for one specific corpus, with genuinely earned rules like tagging variables OBSERVED/INFERRED/ASSUMED and appending `CORRECTION:` inline rather than overwriting; weakest is completeness and code, since the 1,669-byte SKILL.md ships no mechanism at all and its stated quality benchmark (`Anginer_Han_Yildizhan_2025.md`) and update target (`result_summary_comparison.md`) both live outside the skill, so a stranger gets a checklist pointing at files they do not have.
note_c: Standout is product judgment: it specifies concrete evidence, variable, and convention checks for a Hyperliquid literature-review user; weakest is completeness because no executable workflow or worked factsheet is shipped.

name: Canvas Design
author: Anthropic
note_o: Standout is ingenuity — the two-stage inversion (write an art-movement manifesto as a .md first, then have the same model express it), the 'deduce the subtle reference' jazz-quote rule, and the manufactured critique turn ('The user ALREADY said it isn't perfect enough') that forces a refinement pass are prompt-level tricks worth stealing; weakest is completeness, because the SKILL.md tells the model to 'search the ./canvas-fonts directory' for typefaces but the inventory holds only 27 OFL license .txt files and no font binaries, and no rendering toolchain for the required .pdf/.png output is ever named.
note_c: Standout is the attempt to turn a brief into a reusable visual philosophy before execution; weakest is that no canvas-generation mechanism accompanies its promise of polished PNG/PDF artifacts.

name: setup-pre-commit
author: Matt Pocock
note_o: Standout is organization and product discipline — 2.3k across two files with one job each, package-manager detection from the lockfile, .prettierrc written only if none exists, the typecheck/test lines dropped (and the user told) when those scripts are absent, and a final commit used deliberately as the smoke test for the hooks just installed; weakest is difficulty and ingenuity, because this is the documented husky + lint-staged quickstart with no point where an engineer would have to stop and think.
note_c: Standout is a short, navigable setup path that adapts commands to package-manager and script availability; weakest is the instruction to stage and commit changes without confirmation, alongside thin handling of existing repository configurations.

name: Defuddle
author: Steph Ango (kepano)
note_o: Standout is product judgment: 1,123 bytes that state the moment of use, the reason (token savings over WebFetch), a hard default (`--md` always), and a negative trigger sharp enough to be actionable ('Do NOT use for URLs ending in .md'); weakest is difficulty and code, since it is a thin wrapper over one `defuddle parse` invocation with no artifact of the author's own and no named failure modes (paywalls, JS-rendered pages, non-zero exits) for a tool whose whole job is fetching hostile third-party pages.
note_c: Its standout is a sharply scoped default command and explicit .md exception, while ingenuity is weak because it is a thin wrapper around one external CLI invocation.

name: Documentation and ADRs
author: Addy Osmani
note_o: Standout is the 'Match the existing convention first' section, the one agent-aware original idea here -- inspect for existing ADRs, `.adr-dir`, MADR or adr-tools layouts and continue the existing numbering rather than restarting at 001, and surface a conflict instead of silently introducing a second scheme; weakest is code/difficulty, since this is 9.8KB of conventional documentation advice with illustrative TypeScript and OpenAPI fragments but no executable artifact and no stuck point for a competent engineer.
note_c: Completeness is strongest through concrete ADR, API, README, and changelog examples; ingenuity is weakest because the guidance is a conventional documentation checklist without a distinctive mechanism.

name: Redesign Existing Projects
author: Leon (Leonxlnx)
note_o: Standout is the one sharp idea — naming the 'AI design fingerprint' concretely (purple/blue gradient, three equal card columns, Lucide icons, 'Elevate/Seamless' copy, fake-round 99.99% data) and pairing each with a specific replacement, with current CSS knowledge on show (min-height:100dvh over 100vh, text-wrap:balance, transform over top/left); weakest is completeness and organization — one 15KB monolith of roughly 150 undifferentiated bullets with no prioritization, no before/after example, and no executable artifact.
note_c: Product judgment stands out in calling out concrete accessibility and interaction states, while code is weakest because the one-file artifact is a broad stylistic checklist rather than an implemented redesign system.

name: Executing Plans
author: Jesse Vincent (obra)
note_o: Standout is product restraint — 2.3KB, a tight three-step loop with named stop conditions and a header that honestly routes the reader to subagent-driven-development when subagents exist; weakest is completeness and difficulty, since it is a checklist with no mechanism that hard-depends on three sibling skills (using-git-worktrees, finishing-a-development-branch, subagent-driven-development) not shipped alongside it.
note_c: Product judgment stands out in explicit worktree and blocker safeguards, while ingenuity is weakest because the workflow is a conventional sequential execution checklist.

name: Planning and Task Breakdown
author: Addy Osmani
note_o: Standout is product judgment: it names a 'When NOT to use' (single-file changes, specs that already contain tasks), fixes concrete output paths at tasks/plan.md and tasks/todo.md because downstream `/build` tooling expects them, and gives a sizing table with an explicit XL = break-it-down rule; weakest is completeness — the skill is a single 7.6KB prose file whose closing 'See Also' points at `references/definition-of-done.md`, which is not among the shipped files, and there is no worked example showing a real spec turned into a real plan, only templates.
note_c: Its standout is practical product framing through vertical slices, checkpoints, and acceptance criteria, while code quality is absent because it ships only planning prose and templates.

name: Marketing Psychology
author: Corey Haines
note_o: Standout is completeness relative to its class — evals/evals.json ships concrete prompts with per-case assertion lists ('Checks for product-marketing.md', 'Applies Good-Better-Best framing'), which is a testable definition of correct behavior most prose skills never write down; weakest is ingenuity, as the body is ~50 well-known biases and Munger-style mental models each followed by a one-line obvious application, presented as the skill's own taxonomy with no sourcing and no mechanism behind any of it.
note_c: Standout is the inclusion of scenario-specific evaluation cases and ethical framing; weakest is a conventional catalog of named biases with no mechanism, evidence model, or runnable evaluation harness.

name: Using Superpowers
author: Jesse Vincent (obra)
note_o: Standout is organization — a 3KB entry doc routing to one small reference per harness, with genuinely researched details (Antigravity's manage_task is not a todo tool, Gemini's ~/.agents/skills takes precedence over ~/.gemini/skills); weakest is difficulty and completeness together, because the skill is an all-caps compliance harangue ('You cannot rationalize your way out of this') that mandates invoking a skill before even a clarifying question, with zero mechanism, zero executable artifact, and no demonstration that any of it changes behavior.
note_c: The standout is clear cross-harness tool mapping, while the weakest is code because the skill is entirely a rigid process checklist with no executable mechanism.

name: caveman-stats
author: Julius Brussee
note_o: Standout is ingenuity — the hook returns `decision: "block"` with the formatted stats as the reason so the model never computes (or hallucinates) the numbers, and it subtracts estimated per-turn rule-injection overhead to report a net that can be negative and says so plainly instead of hiding behind gross savings; weakest is completeness — the entire mechanism lives in `hooks/caveman-stats.js` and `docs/HONEST-NUMBERS.md`, neither shipped in the skill, so the 1.1KB file is a pointer with no runnable content or sample output.
note_c: The net-savings calculation that exposes rule overhead shows good product honesty; the hook that supposedly produces every result is not included.

name: Migrate to Shoehorn
author: Matt Pocock
note_o: Standout is completeness for its size — install command, a concrete find step (`grep -r " as [A-Z]" --include="*.test.ts"`), before/after pairs for each pattern and a type-check verification close; weakest is ingenuity and difficulty — it is the package README restated as a three-row mapping table (`as Type`→fromPartial, `as unknown as`→fromAny), with a 'gather requirements, ask the user' phase bolted onto what is a mechanical grep-and-replace.
note_c: Concrete before-and-after migration examples make the intended user clear; the workflow is otherwise a thin wrapper around an existing library with no automation.

name: minimalist-ui
author: Leon (Leonxlnx)
note_o: The banned-elements framing is the best part — defining taste by negating LLM defaults (no Inter, no Lucide, no shadow-lg, no 'Elevate/Seamless/Unleash' copy, no Lorem Ipsum) is specific and enforceable; completeness is the weakest, with no worked output, no prerequisites, no failure modes, and an internal contradiction where section 2 bans gradients outright while sections 6 and 7 prescribe radial-gradient light spots and a drifting ambient gradient blob.
note_c: Its strongest evidence is a coherent and concrete visual system with CSS-level constraints; difficulty is weakest because it is a style checklist without an implementation mechanism.

name: paper-reading-site-editor
author: Xin (applicant)
note_o: Standout is product judgment — scope is cut hard to two fields with a byte-preservation rule ('Do not modify any other byte') and a precise negative-space list (no coefficients, t-statistics, basis points, Greek symbols, LaTeX) that reads as learned from real failures; weakest is completeness, with no sample JSON, no schema, no validator, and no path to the paper-site files a stranger would need.
note_c: The standout is sharply constrained product scope around preserving claims while editing two presentation fields, while the weakest is code because JSON preservation is instructed but not implemented.

name: Find Skills
author: Vercel Labs
note_o: Completeness is the relative standout — every command is real and copy-pasteable (`npx skills find`, `add`, `init`) and the no-results path is written out with example copy; code is weakest, with no executable artifact whatsoever and the whole skill reducing to prose around one CLI, while `npx skills add <owner/repo@skill> -g -y` installs third-party agent instructions globally with confirmation suppressed.
note_c: The standout is a readable discovery-to-verification flow, while the weakest is code quality because the skill contains no executable mechanism beyond instructing the agent to invoke an external CLI.

name: sector-map
author: Xin (applicant)
note_o: Standout is product judgment — the field rules make real decisions instead of exposing options (Multi-chain only at 3+ chains with no primary, Bootstrapped vs Not disclosed) and the one-line-no-sub-bullets format is a deliberate cut; weakest is code/difficulty, a single 2KB markdown output template with no executable artifact and a hard dependency on an unshipped /project-research stage.
note_c: Standout product judgment: the one-line project format and funding/ecosystem defaults fit a specific sourcing handoff; weakest code quality: the submission is only a prose checklist with no executable artifact.

name: Brandkit
author: Leon (Leonxlnx)
note_o: Standout is product, in that it does commit to defaults (3x3 board, 4:3, a fixed nine-panel system) and bans specific failure modes ("no generic lightning bolts", "no meaningless sparkles"); weakest is completeness, since a 16KB single SKILL.md never names what actually renders the image, ships no example input or output, and stacks nine visual-mode taxonomies with no way to verify any of it.
note_c: Its strongest evidence is a coherent board-and-symbol art-direction framework with deliberate defaults, while code quality is absent because the sole artifact is a monolithic generation prompt.

name: Theme Factory
author: Anthropic
note_o: Standout is organization: a 3KB entry doc routing to ten ~520-byte theme files is textbook progressive disclosure with resources cleanly separated from instructions; weakest is completeness, because step 1 of the documented workflow is "Display the theme-showcase.pdf file" and that file is absent from the shipped inventory, so the prescribed first action fails.
note_c: Organization is strongest in the separate, consistently named theme specifications, while completeness is weakest because the required theme-showcase PDF is referenced but absent from the shipped inventory.

name: Writing Guidelines
author: Vercel Labs
note_o: Standout is organization, in the trivial sense that a 1.2KB single file has one obvious place for everything; weakest is difficulty — the entire mechanism is one WebFetch of a raw GitHub URL whose fetched content supplies the rules, the output format, and the judgment, with no cache, no offline path, and no handling of a failed fetch.
note_c: Standout: fetching a fresh canonical guide before review makes the intended documentation-audit user and stale-rule tradeoff clear; weakest: it blindly treats remote fetched content as instructions and supplies no implementation or validation of the review process.

name: project-research
author: Xin (applicant)
note_o: Standout is product judgment: the structured record template plus 'Not disclosed beats guessing' and the flag-unfunded-projects-as-early-signal heuristic show a real VC-analyst user in mind; weakest is code, which is two inline curl calls to RootData and a Twitter proxy with no script, no parsing of the responses, and an acknowledged 401 on the free tier that is left to prose fallback.
note_c: Standout: the record schema and explicit treatment of undisclosed funding make the intended quick-DD user legible; weakest: it is only a checklist with two credentialed curl snippets, with no implementation for discovery, synthesis, or safely handling fetched tweet/search content.

name: Web Design Guidelines
author: Vercel Labs
note_o: Standout is the one deliberate decision — refusing to vendor the guidelines and instead WebFetching raw.githubusercontent.com/vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines/main/command.md fresh on every run, so the skill cannot drift from the canonical source; weakest is difficulty and completeness, since the entire 1231-byte file is a pointer with no mechanism, no fallback when the fetch fails or the URL moves, and by its own words the fetched remote content 'contains all the rules and output format instructions' that are then followed verbatim.
note_c: Standout product judgment is the narrowly scoped file-and-line review workflow with fresh guidelines; weakest code quality is that all substantive review rules are delegated to an unpinned remote document rather than implemented in the skill.

name: research
author: Matt Pocock
note_o: Standout is product judgment: three sentences with a real opinion — delegate to a background agent so the foreground keeps working, chase every claim to the source that owns it, and match the repo's existing notes convention — with no filler; weakest is difficulty, since 799 bytes of instruction contain no mechanism whatsoever and a strong engineer has nowhere to get stuck.
note_c: Standout: it insists on tracing claims back to primary owners and saving one cited repo-local note; weakest: the entire mechanism is an instruction to delegate, without a concrete research, citation, or file-placement implementation.

name: Using Agent Skills
author: Addy Osmani
note_o: Standout is the operating-behaviors section, which at least takes a position ('sycophancy is a failure mode', 'if you build 1000 lines and 100 would suffice, you have failed'); weakest is completeness and organization — the single shipped file routes to ~24 sibling skills and cites references/definition-of-done.md, none of which exist here, and the same routing information is repeated three times as an ASCII decision tree, a 16-step lifecycle, and a quick-reference table.
note_c: Standout is the compact lifecycle map that makes engineering phases legible; weakest is that claimed skill discovery and governing behavior reduce to static prose and reference an unshipped definition-of-done file.

name: GPT Taste
author: Leon (Leonxlnx)
note_o: Standout is the failure-mode diagnosis — narrow containers causing 6-line H1 wraps, dead bento cells fixed with grid-flow-dense, invisible button text, 'SECTION 01' meta-labels — which reads as observed taste rather than generic advice; weakest is difficulty, because the headline mechanism, 'PYTHON-DRIVEN TRUE RANDOMIZATION', explicitly instructs the model to *simulate* a script and 'write a 3-line mock Python output', so the central claim has no mechanism behind it at all.
note_c: Standout organization: the visual prescriptions are grouped into a readable checklist; weakest completeness/code: it claims Python-driven true randomization while providing neither Python nor an implementation mechanism.

name: Anthropic Brand Guidelines
author: Anthropic
note_o: Standout is product, in a thin sense: a palette of seven hex tokens plus two font choices is genuinely zero-configuration and a stranger can apply it immediately; weakest is code and difficulty — the 'Features' and 'Technical Details' sections describe Smart Font Application, automatic Arial/Georgia fallback, background-aware color selection and shapes cycling through accents 'applied via python-pptx's RGBColor class', but the skill ships only SKILL.md and an Apache LICENSE that is five times its size, so every one of those mechanisms is a claim with nothing behind it.
note_c: Its standout is concise organization of a small style reference, while code quality is absent despite SKILL.md claiming automatic font and RGBColor application without shipping a mechanism.

name: Grill With Docs
author: Matt Pocock
note_o: Standout is product judgment only in the narrow sense that disable-model-invocation: true is a deliberate choice to make this user-triggered; weakest is essentially everything else — the entire skill body is one sentence ("Run a /grilling session, using the /domain-modeling skill") that delegates to two artifacts not shipped here, so the description's promise of a relentless interview producing ADRs and a glossary has no mechanism behind it.
note_c: The only positive is a concise composition intent, while completeness is weakest because the promised grilling and documentation behavior is delegated to unshipped external skills with no operational instructions here.

name: Grill Me
author: Matt Pocock
note_o: Standout, faintly, is organization: two tiny files with a coherent split between the skill body and the openai.yaml interface, where `disable-model-invocation: true` and `allow_implicit_invocation: false` agree with each other as a deliberate explicit-invocation-only choice; weakest is completeness — the entire body is 'Run a `/grilling` session.', a command that ships nowhere in the skill, so the promised 'relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design' does not exist as a mechanism and cannot run in a stranger's hands.
note_c: Its standout is minimal discoverability metadata, while completeness is zero because the entire implementation is an unresolved instruction to run /grilling.

name: Template Skill
author: Anthropic
note_o: Standout, such as it is, is organization — the single 140-byte file is at least internally consistent frontmatter plus a heading; weakest is essentially everything else, since the entire content is the placeholder strings "Replace with description of the skill" and "# Insert instructions below", carrying no mechanism, decision, or demonstration.
note_c: Standout organization: the minimal frontmatter identifies the intended slot for a skill; weakest completeness: the sole file is an unfilled placeholder with no behavior, example, or runnable artifact.
